narrative: Re : Formal Dispute of Charge-Off Status Potential 1099-C Cancellation of Debt Reporting Violation Account Name : Experian, Transunion, Equifax To Whom It May Concern, This is a formal dispute under my rights granted by the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), 15 U.S. Code 1681i and 15 U.S. Code 1681s-2, demanding an immediate investigation and removal of the charge-off status currently being reported on my credit profile for the above-referenced account. ISSUE : Illegal Continuation of Reporting a Charged-Off Account Potentially Forgiven via 1099-C It has come to my attention that this creditor may have filed an IRS Form 1099-C ( Cancellation of Debt ) for this alleged debt. Under IRS regulations ( IRS Pub. 4681 ), a 1099-C filing signifies that the creditor has legally canceled the debt, which classifies it as forgiven income for the borrower and effectively terminates the creditors ability to pursue collection or continue to report the debt as active or delinquent. If this is the case, continued reporting of the account as a charge-off or open collection is inaccurate and misleading, and violates both IRS regulations and the FCRA 's requirement for accurate, complete, and verifiable reporting. RELEVANT LAWS AND REGULATORY FRAMEWORK 15 USC 1681i Credit reporting agencies must reinvestigate and correct any information that is inaccurate, incomplete, or unverifiable. 15 USC 1681s-2 ( a ) Furnishers are required to provide accurate data and must not report information that is known to be incorrect. IRS Pub. 4681 Once a creditor files a 1099-C, the debt is considered discharged and is no longer legally collectible. Federal Trade Commission ( FTC ) & IRS Both agencies have clarified that post-1099-C collection attempts or negative credit reporting can amount to deceptive and unlawful practices. DEMAND FOR INVESTIGATION Pursuant to the above, I demand the following : Full reinvestigation of the charge-off account listed above. Immediate removal of the charge-off status and any related derogatory remarks if a 1099-C was filed. Written confirmation of whether the creditor has filed a Form 1099-C with the IRS. If no 1099-C has been filed, I demand certified documentation verifying the current collectible status and balance, including : A full accounting ledger showing the charge-off and post-charge-off activity. Written confirmation of the creditor 's intent regarding tax reporting or abandonment of collection. Chain of title and proof of continued right to report and collect. ADDITIONAL POINTS If a 1099-C was issued, the creditor has voluntarily canceled the debt and reported it as such to the IRS. Therefore, continuing to list this account as an unpaid charge-off or delinquent balance is double-dippingattempting to benefit from both a tax deduction and continued reporting/collection. This practice is not only misleading but may expose the data furnisher and the credit bureau to regulatory penalties and civil liability under 15 USC 1681n and 1681o. FAILURE TO ACT Should you fail to correct or delete this inaccurate reporting within the legally mandated timeframe, I will not hesitate to : File a complaint with the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ) Notify the Federal Trade Commission ( FTC ) File a formal complaint with the IRS regarding unlawful dual reporting/collection on canceled debt Seek legal counsel for damages under the FCRA for negligent or willful noncompliance CONCLUSION This is a serious matter that must be resolved in compliance with both federal tax law and consumer credit law. I expect to receive written confirmation of the outcome of this reinvestigation, including a clear explanation of whether or not a 1099-C was filed and the legal status of the alleged debt. Thank you for your prompt attention. Please consider this letter a formal dispute under my rights afforded by the FCRA and IRS guidelines. Sincerely, XXXX XXXX

narrative: on XXXX XXXX i noticed a debt collection issued on my credit as a result of identity theft i ask that it please be removed!!!! 15 USC 1681b is a section of the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), which is a federal law that regulates the collection, use, and dissemination of consumer credit information by credit reporting agencies. Section 15 USC 1681b specifically addresses the permissible purposes for which consumer credit reports can be accessed and used by third parties. Under 15 USC 1681b, credit reporting agencies are only allowed to furnish consumer credit reports to those who have a permissible purpose as defined by the FCRA. Permissible purposes for accessing and using consumer credit reports include : Credit transactions : When a consumer applies for credit, such as a loan, credit card, or mortgage, the creditor has a permissible purpose to request and obtain the consumer 's credit report to assess their creditworthiness. Employment purposes : Employers may request and obtain consumer credit reports for employment purposes, but only with the written consent of the consumer. This typically applies to positions that require financial responsibility or access to sensitive financial information. Insurance underwriting : Insurance companies may request and obtain consumer credit reports for underwriting purposes, such as determining rates and eligibility for insurance coverage. Court orders and legal requirements : Credit reports may be accessed and used in response to a court order, subpoena, or other legal requirement. Legitimate business needs : Other legitimate business needs, as defined by the FCRA, may also constitute permissible purposes for obtaining consumer credit reports. This typically requires a valid reason and compliance with applicable laws and regulations.

issue: Advertising and marketing, including promotional offers
narrative: To the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, I am filing a formal complaint against JPMorgan Chase Bank , N.A . ( JPMCB ) for engaging in deceptive, unfair, and unauthorized practices involving the securitization and sale of my consumer credit card receivablewithout my informed consent, full disclosure, or legal clarity. After approving me for a credit card, JPMCB created a receivable ( the balance I owed ) and transferred it into a trust structure such as Chase Issuance Trust, which then issued asset-backed securities ( ABS ) backed by my obligation. These securities were sold to investors and traded on global secondary markets, all while I was left completely uninformed. Despite monetizing my receivable and no longer holding the beneficial ownership, JPMCB continues to act as if it owns my accountreporting it to the credit bureaus and collecting payments. This dual role is deceptive : JPMCB earns investor proceeds by selling my account and simultaneously pursues me for payment without acknowledging the securitization. I was never notified that : My financial obligation would be pooled and securitized, My receivable would be used to create and sell investment-grade securities, JPMCB would profit from the sale while still reporting and enforcing the account as a creditor. These actions are misleading, harmful, and illegal, and they violate multiple consumer protection laws : Violations : Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ), 15 U.S.C. 1601 et seq. JPMCB failed to disclose material facts regarding the true creditor and securitization of the account. Violates 1637 ( a ) ( 6 ) and 1639 ( b ). Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), 15 U.S.C. 1681 et seq. JPMCB may be reporting account information without having legal ownership or standing. Violates 1681s-2 ( b ) and 1681e ( b ). Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act ( GLBA ), 15 U.S.C. 68016809 ; 12 C.F.R. 1016 ( Reg P ) JPMCB shared my private financial data with third-party trusts and investors without providing the opt-out rights required by law. Consumer Financial Protection Act ( CFPA ), 12 U.S.C. 55315536 These acts constitute Unfair, Deceptive, or Abusive Acts or Practices ( UDAAP ). JPMCB concealed the securitization of my obligation and misrepresented their ownership interest. Uniform Commercial Code ( UCC ) UCC 3-301 : Only a holder in due course can enforce the obligationJPMCB may lack standing. UCC 9-210 : No accounting or assignment records were disclosed to me. UCC 9-404 : The assignee ( trust ) is subject to consumer defenses, yet was never disclosed. Due Process Clause ( 5th & 14th Amendments of U.S. Constitution ) I was denied a fair opportunity to dispute or understand how my obligation was altered. Key Evidence : A JPMCB Prospectus Supplement ( SEC XXXX Filing ) confirms that consumer receivablesincluding mineare being packaged into securities and sold to investors, all without informing the originating consumer. This is strong evidence that JPMCB is engaging in systemic nondisclosure and financial misrepresentation. Requested Resolution : I respectfully request the CFPB to : Investigate JPMCB for deceptive, unfair, and unauthorized securitization of consumer accounts ; Require full disclosure to consumers whose credit card accounts have been securitized or transferred into trusts ; Order the deletion of negative credit reporting where JPMCB no longer owns the account ; Prohibit collection activity on receivables that have been sold or securitized without consumer consent ; Award compensation for financial harm, credit damage, emotional distress, and privacy violations ; Refer JPMCB for criminal or regulatory enforcement where applicable.

issue: Attempts to collect debt not owed
narrative: The XXXX XXXX company information is incorrectly reporting to Equifax, XXXX, and XXXX. This account was not charged off as bad debt. According to the The FCRA provides people multiple ways to dispute inaccurate information on their credit reports. Commonly, people dispute the accuracy of information on their credit reports with a credit reporting company, such as XXXX, Equifax, or XXXX. In response, the credit reporting company often refers the dispute to the company that provided the disputed information. When a person submits a dispute to a credit reporting company, and it is passed along to the company that originally provided the disputed information, the company is then required to conduct its own investigation into the disputed information. If a company that provided disputed information to a credit reporting agency is unable to determine whether the information is true or not, the law requires them to tell the credit reporting company the information could not be verified so that the credit reporting company will stop reporting it. Nonetheless, some companies have argued that if they are unable to determine that the disputed information is false, they are free to tell the consumer reporting company to continue providing the information on reports. Thats wrong, as the CFPB and FTCs brief explains. In the FCRA, Congress put express requirements on companies with respect to information that can not be verified. Those requirements would be meaningless if companies could continue providing unverified information and telling credit reporting companies that they could continue sharing it.

To : Consumer Financial Protection Bureau Subject : Complaint Against Westlake Portfolio Management Improper Debt Collection and Vehicle Repossession Following USA Auto Sales Closure Dear CFPB, I am submitting this complaint to formally report Westlake Portfolio Management for alleged improper debt collection practices and unlawful repossession of my vehicle following the sudden closure of USA Auto Sales, from whom I originally purchased the car. After USA Auto Sales went out of business, I was never properly notified that Westlake had taken over my auto loan account. I received no advance communication, notice of debt assignment, or payment instructions before my vehicle was repossessed. I only learned of Westlakes involvement after the repossession had already taken place. This situation has caused me financial distress and appears to violat e multiple consumer protection laws : Georgia law ( O.C.G.A. 11-9-611 ) requires creditors to send notice to borrowers before repossession. Georgia law ( O.C.G.A. 10-1-31 ) also requires transparent communication and lawful handling of retail installment contracts. Under the Federal Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1692g ), a debt collector must provide timely written notice of debt ownership and give the consumer an opportunity to dispute it. I did not receive such notification from Westlake Portfolio prior to the repossession. The Fair Credit Reporting Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ) prohibits the reporting of disputed or unverified debts to credit bureaus, yet I believe this debt may have already been reported against me. I am requesting the CFPBs assistance in investigating this matter and holding Westlake Portfolio accountable for any violations. Specifically, I am asking that : Westlake be required to provide proper documentation proving lawful acquisition of my account. Westlake provide proof that required notices were sent prior to repossession. Any negative credit reporting be suspended or removed until proper investigation is completed. The repossession and debt be evaluated for legal compliance. I have attached any relevant documents I have ( if applicable ), but much of the confusion lies in the lack of communication and documentation from the companies involved. Please investigate this matter and ensure that my rights under Georgia and federal consumer laws are upheld.

issue: Applying for a mortgage or refinancing an existing mortgage
narrative: Previously in this form, it mentions that you may send my complaint directly to Rocket Mortgage. Contacting them is the last thing I want to do because they hold the recorded conversations. That is the only evidence I have in the crimes Im about to explain. With that being said, I need those phone calls subpoenaed. All of the crimes and laws that were broken were done verbally on those taped recorded calls. Having the calls in our possession is our only defense. Without the calls, theres a chance of them getting away with many crimes. The crimes that I believed that they are committing fall under predatory lending. Around XXXX of XXXX, I contacted Rocket Mortgage to inquire about a loan. Somehow, I ended up in negotiations with a woman about mortgaging my wifes house that she inherited. I believe this to be one of the crimes. From my research, the mortgage company can not negotiate with me about a mortgage on a house I do not own. They were supposed to gain written permission from my wife before ever speaking with me which they did not receive. ( I did not find out this about information until recently. ) During these conversations, the woman I was speaking with kept mentioning that I could recast this loan after 3 to 6 months ( I cant be certain on the amount of time ). She mentioned that I could drastically reduce the amount of my payment by doing this recast. I cant be certain on the exact details, but when I called about a year later to inquire about the recast ( around XX/XX/XXXX ), I spoke with a different representative and they told me that the recast would involve me putting down a large sum of money, however, the note was only going to go down a very little bit. I believe the reason the first representative mentioned the recast, was as a way to lure me into signing the original mortgage. The second representative said that a refinance would be better than a recast. ( I believe this to be a part of the big scam luring you in with the hopes of a recast and lowering the note, but then talking you into a refinance. ) I would like to point out here, that during the course of this loan, I would end up in phone conversations with several different representatives. During one of these conversations, I was on the phone with a gentlemen who gave me the option to borrow more money. I believe the highest offer I received was around {$80000.00} or more. He used phrases like isnt more money better than less money and would I lie to you, etc. From my research, offering me money that I didnt asked for or need is a crime. I believe this is called unsolicited lending. I also believe this is a part of the predatory lending where they offer me more money to put me in a position that will result in me defaulting on the loan and the mortgage company repossessing the house. Eventually, I ended up being talked into refinancing because I was promised a lower interest rate, they would knock 10 years off the loan, I was also getting a lower note and I would receive approximately {$3000.00} back. However, each time I called during this process, different people would answer the phone and give me conflicting information on the amount of money back or what my new loan amount would be, etc. Those figures changed with each phone call. At some point we were asked to sign papers in our Rocket portal. I remember being reluctant in signing these papers, because the numbers didnt look correct. Im not 100 % sure, but I think I remember them saying they needed the papers signed to go forward with the refinance and that those numbers were going to change the closer we got to closing. I do remember that each time I called, the amount of cash I was supposed to receive back at closing changed. It went from {$3000.00} to {$1000.00} to {$0.00} then back to {$1500.00} ( figures are approximate ). Im also not 100 % sure, but I seem to remember talking to someone about backing out if I couldnt get the {$3000.00} that was originally promised. To try and sum this up, when we went to sign the papers, the stack was about a foot tall. I believe this was an intimidation tactic so that we wouldnt read the papers. A key point that I need to point out, was that we were rushed throughout this entire process. Hurry up and lock in the loan while the interest rate is this low or youre going to miss it. In the end, we did receive the lower interest rate and 10 years was knocked off the loan ; however, we did not receive {$3000.00} ( we received a lower amount ) and the note was not lower. This is another part of the scam. This is how I believe it works giving us the lower interest rate and them reminding me that Im saving {$100000.00} in interest payments, is a distraction to get me to refinance. All the while, my note stayed basically the same because they know that my note is the maximum that my salary can afford. The 10 years off is actually because I didnt accept one of the larger amounts. It was actually protecting Rocket Mortgage from losing 10 years of equity. Why would they take {$100000.00} off the loan when I was already locked in and I wasnt complaining? And by refinancing after one year of the loan, the majority of my payment is still going to the interest and not the principal. I think Ive given you enough information to start. We can always discuss this further. I suspect that Rocket Mortgage is a company that only exists on paper. They have no physical branches and you can not speak to the lender. I also suspect that they are a front for some type of criminal organization. They do legitimate business involving large sums of money, kickbacks and payoffs all to distract the authorities. If they are investigated, it would seem that they would look at the large sums of money that was loaned out instead of the small sums of money that was obtained using predatory lending. They prey on individuals that are handicapped, elderly, low income, and do not understand the terms of the loan. This is so that in the case one of these individuals does realize theyve been scammed, they will accept a settlement rather than bringing them to court. This may seem like a large amount to the individual that is being scammed but is just a small drop in the bucket for Rocket Mortgage. I would compare it to Loan Sharking. This is just my opinion or my theory. In closing, thats why its important to obtain those phone calls to see if there is something that I may have missed or left out. Im not doing this for money. I have nothing and if I end up with nothing, Im used to it. They have a lot to lose.

narrative: On XX/XX/year>, I called a business I believed to be XXXX, which is the XXXX XXXX XXXX company. This is how they identified themselves when they answered my call. I tried to call the number I used for the original call to try to get an email confirmation, but that number actually was for XXXX and they told me they had no record of the phone call I described or the {$2500.00} transaction. I then tried to call the phone number listed on my WF account for this transaction, but I found the phone was never answered. I tried many times on different days. I knew then that I had been defrauded, so I opened a claim at WF fraud department. They temporarily reversed the charge on the card and then investigated. In a couple of months they told me my claim was denied because the merchant responded to their satisfaction. I could not believe that so I requested WF send me all information received from XXXX XXXX regarding this dispute. They sent it, and I saw the following evidence of fraud : 1. XXXX XXXX claims it was a transaction on their website, but really it was over the phone. 2. They claim it was for an airline ticket, but really it was for homeowner insurance. 3. They provided zero detailed information regarding the alleged airline ticket : no airline, no itinerary, no ticket copy, absolutely nothing that a legitimate travel business would provide if the ticket actually existed. 4. They gave a confirmation number, but a confirmation number only has meaning to a specific airline, so this number meant nothing. 5. They indicated they sent the email confirmation of the purchase to an email address that I do not own, have never used, and did not know existed. It is fake. 6. They provided a forged signature of mine used to give my permission for electronic signature. I understand it's not a a real signature, but I never filled out any such form, which makes that signature a forgery. 7. They provided an alleged email sent by one of their employees, a " XXXX XXXX ''. This is clearly a fake name used for the purpose of defrauding people. 8. They provided what is supposed to be a confirmation email they sent to me, but this email has every indication of scam. It contains absolutely no verifiable information except my identity and my card number and address. Absolutely no evidence of the transaction they claim occurred. I spoke to a WF agent who agreed with me that these things were very troubling, so she kept the claim open and moved it to a second stage. After multiple days I received another notice they were rejecting my claim. I called WF again. This agent was not sympathetic to me at all. Here is what she said : 1. There is a fine difference between fraud and scam. The difference is that scam occurs when you give your card number willingly to someone who is lying to you. When that happens, Wells Fargo will never back you up because it's your fault, so you're on your own. She said if XXXX XXXX had gotten my card number by some other means then WF would help me, but since it's my fault they won't. 2. She told me that the claim that was opened wasn't for fraud. Wells Fargo opened a completely different claim than I had requested. The claim had nothing to do with fraud or scam. Wells Fargo contended that I had cancelled the airline ticket and not received a refund. That was a complete misrepresentation of the claim I opened, and WF had lied to me from the start. 3. Since the claim was centered on cancelling the nonexistent airline ticket, XXXX XXXX was never reqquired to provide the actual ticket. They only had to provide a statement saying I did not cancel the ticket within the required timeframe. And WF took what they said as fact. 4. She told me Wells Fargo acknowledges the evidence of fraud I indicated, and they will not stand behind me anyway. I again requested a better investigation, and a few days later I was told by phone call that my claim was escalated to round 3, and it would take more time to complete. I waited weeks and then received the notice that the claim was rejected again, the third time, and the information they sent me from XXXX XXXX is identical to the first round of information. Once again, the evidence of fraud is overwhelming ; the evidence of a valid ticket is absent. I disagree that this is not fraud. When you agree on the phone to a transaction for one product which you never receive, but instead are accused of making a completely different transaction you never made, that is fraud.

( B ) Reporting information after notice and confirmation of errors A person shall not furnish information relating to a consumer to any consumer reporting agency if ( i ) the person has been notified by the consumer, at the address specified by the person for such notices, that specific information is inaccurate; and ( ii ) the information is, in fact, inaccurate. ( C ) No address requirement A person who clearly and conspicuously specifies to the consumer an address for notices referred to in subparagraph ( B ) shall not be subject to subparagraph ( A ) ; however, nothing in subparagraph ( B ) shall require a person to specify such an address. ( D ) Definition For purposes of subparagraph ( A ), the term reasonable cause to believe that the information is inaccurate means having specific knowledge, other than solely allegations by the consumer, that would cause a reasonable person to have substantial doubts about the accuracy of the information. ( E ) Rehabilitation of private education loans ( i ) In general Notwithstanding any other provision of this section, a consumer may request a financial institution to remove from a consumer report a reported default regarding a private education loan, and such information shall not be considered inaccurate, if ( I ) the financial institution chooses to offer a loan rehabilitation program which includes, without limitation, a requirement of the consumer to make consecutive on-time monthly payments in a number that demonstrates, in the assessment of the financial institution offering the loan rehabilitation program, a renewed ability and willingness to repay the loan ; and ( II ) the requirements of the loan rehabilitation program described in subclause ( I ) are successfully met. ( ii ) Banking agencies ( I ) In general If a financial institution is supervised by a Federal banking agency, the financial institution shall seek written approval concerning the terms and conditions of the loan rehabilitation program described in clause ( i ) from the appropriate Federal banking agency. ( II ) Feedback An appropriate Federal banking agency shall provide feedback to a financial institution within 120 days of a request for approval under subclause ( I ). ( iii ) Limitation ( I ) In general A consumer may obtain the benefits available under this subsection with respect to rehabilitating a loan only 1 time per loan. ( II ) Rule of construction Nothing in this subparagraph may be construed to require a financial institution to offer a loan rehabilitation program or to remove any reported default from a consumer report as a consideration of a loan rehabilitation program, except as described in clause ( i ). ( iv ) Definitions For purposes of this subparagraph ( I ) the term appropriate Federal banking agency has the meaning given the term in section 1813 of title 12 ; and ( II ) the term private education loan has the meaning given the term in section 1650 ( a ) of this title. ( F ) Reporting information during XXXX pandemic ( i ) Definitions In this subsection : ( I ) Accommodation The term accommodation includes an agreement to defer XXXX or more payments, make a partial payment, forbear any delinquent amounts, modify a loan or contract, or any other assistance or relief granted to a consumer who is affected by the coronavirus XXXX XXXX ( XXXX ) pandemic during the covered period. ( XXXX ) Covered period The term covered period means the period beginning on XX/XX/XXXX and ending on the later of ( aa ) 120 days after XX/XX/XXXX ; or ( XXXX ) 120 days after the date on which the national emergency concerning the novel coronavirus XXXX ( XXXX ) outbreak declared by the President on XX/XX/XXXX under the National Emergencies Act ( 50 U.S.C. 1601 et seq. ) terminates. ( ii ) Reporting Except as provided in clause ( iii ), if a furnisher makes an accommodation with respect to 1 or more payments on a credit obligation or account of a consumer, and the consumer makes the payments or is not required to make 1 or more payments pursuant to the accommodation, the furnisher shall ( I ) report the credit obligation or account as current; or ( II ) if the credit obligation or account was delinquent before the accommodation ( aa ) maintain the delinquent status during the period in which the accommodation is in effect; and ( bb ) if the consumer brings the credit obligation or account current during the period described in item ( aa ), report the credit obligation or account as current. ( iii ) Exception Clause ( ii ) shall not apply with respect to a credit obligation or account of a consumer that has been charged-off. ( 2 ) Duty to correct and update information A person who ( A ) regularly and in the ordinary course of business furnishes information to one or more consumer reporting agencies about the persons transactions or experiences with any consumer ; and ( B ) has furnished to a consumer reporting agency information that the person determines is not complete or accurate, shall promptly notify the consumer reporting agency of that determination and provide to the agency any corrections to that information, or any additional information, that is necessary to make the information provided by the person to the agency complete and accurate, and shall not thereafter furnish to the agency any of the information that remains not complete or accurate. ( 3 ) Duty to provide notice of dispute If the completeness or accuracy of any information furnished by any person to any consumer reporting agency is disputed to such person by a consumer, the person may not furnish the information to any consumer reporting agency without notice that such information is disputed by the consumer. ( 4 ) Duty to provide notice of closed accounts A person who regularly and in the ordinary course of business furnishes information to a consumer reporting agency regarding a consumer who has a credit account with that person shall notify the agency of the voluntary closure of the account by the consumer, in information regularly furnished for the period in which the account is closed. ( 5 ) Duty to provide notice of delinquency of accounts ( A ) In general A person who furnishes information to a consumer reporting agency regarding a delinquent account being placed for collection, charged to profit or loss, or subjected to any similar action shall, not later than 90 days after furnishing the information, notify the agency of the date of delinquency on the account, which shall be the month and year of the commencement of the delinquency on the account that immediately preceded the action. ( B ) Rule of construction For purposes of this paragraph only, and provided that the consumer does not dispute the information, a person that furnishes information on a delinquent account that is placed for collection, charged for profit or loss, or subjected to any similar action, complies with this paragraph, if ( i ) the person reports the same date of delinquency as that provided by the creditor to which the account was owed at the time at which the commencement of the delinquency occurred, if the creditor previously reported that date of delinquency to a consumer reporting agency ; ( ii ) the creditor did not previously report the date of delinquency to a consumer reporting agency, and the person establishes and follows reasonable procedures to obtain the date of delinquency from the creditor or another reliable source and reports that date to a consumer reporting agency as the date of delinquency ; or ( iii ) the creditor did not previously report the date of delinquency to a consumer reporting agency and the date of delinquency can not be reasonably obtained as provided in clause ( ii ), the person establishes and follows reasonable procedures to ensure the date reported as the date of delinquency precedes the date on which the account is placed for collection, charged to profit or loss, or subjected to any similar action, and reports such date to the credit reporting agency. ( 6 ) Duties of furnishers upon notice of identity theft-related information ( A ) Reasonable procedures A person that furnishes information to any consumer reporting agency shall have in place reasonable procedures to respond to any notification that it receives from a consumer reporting agency under section 1681c2 of this title relating to information resulting from identity theft, to prevent that person from refurnishing such blocked information. ( B ) Information alleged to result from identity theft If a consumer submits an identity theft report to a person who furnishes information to a consumer reporting agency at the address specified by that person for receiving such reports stating that information maintained by such person that purports to relate to the consumer resulted from identity theft, the person may not furnish such information that purports to relate to the consumer to any consumer reporting agency, unless the person subsequently knows or is informed by the consumer that the information is correct. ( 7 ) Negative information ( A ) Notice to consumer required ( i ) In general If any financial institution that extends credit and regularly and in the ordinary course of business furnishes information to a consumer reporting agency described in section 1681a ( p ) of this title furnishes negative information to such an agency regarding credit extended to a customer, the financial institution shall provide a notice of such furnishing of negative information, in writing, to the customer. ( ii ) Notice effective for subsequent submissions After providing such notice, the financial institution may submit additional negative information to a consumer reporting agency described in section 1681a ( p ) of this title with respect to the same transaction, extension of credit, account, or customer without providing additional notice to the customer. ( B ) Time of notice ( i ) In general The notice required under subparagraph ( A ) shall be provided to the customer prior to, or no later than 30 days after, furnishing the negative information to a consumer reporting agency described in section 1681a ( p ) of this title. ( ii ) Coordination with new account disclosures If the notice is provided to the customer prior to furnishing the negative information to a consumer reporting agency, the notice may not be included in the initial disclosures provided under section 1637 ( a ) of this title. ( C ) Coordination with other disclosures The notice required under subparagraph ( A ) ( i ) may be included on or with any notice of default, any billing statement, or any other materials provided to the customer; and ( ii ) must be clear and conspicuous. ( D ) Model disclosure ( i ) Duty of Bureau The Bureau shall prescribe a brief model disclosure that a financial institution may use to comply with subparagraph ( A ), which shall not exceed 30 words. ( ii ) Use of model not required No provision of this paragraph may be construed to require a financial institution to use any such model form prescribed by the Bureau. ( iii ) Compliance using model A financial institution shall be deemed to be in compliance with subparagraph ( A ) if the financial institution uses any model form prescribed by the Bureau under this subparagraph, or the financial institution uses any such model form and rearranges its format. ( E ) Use of notice without submitting negative information No provision of this paragraph shall be construed as requiring a financial institution that has provided a customer with a notice described in subparagraph ( A ) to furnish negative information about the customer to a consumer reporting agency. ( F ) Safe harbor A financial institution shall not be liable for failure to perform the duties required by this paragraph if, at the time of the failure, the financial institution maintained reasonable policies and procedures to comply with this paragraph or the financial institution reasonably believed that the institution is prohibited, by law, from contacting the consumer. ( G ) Definitions For purposes of this paragraph, the following definitions shall apply : ( i ) Negative information The term negative information means information concerning a customers delinquencies, late payments, insolvency, or any form of default. ( ii ) Customer ; financial institution The terms customer and financial institution have the same meanings as in section 6809 of this title. ( 8 ) Ability of consumer to dispute information directly with furnisher ( A ) In general The Bureau, in consultation with the Federal Trade Commission, the Federal banking agencies, and the National Credit Union Administration, shall prescribe regulations that shall identify the circumstances under which a furnisher shall be required to reinvestigate a dispute concerning the accuracy of information contained in a consumer report on the consumer, based on a direct request of a consumer. ( B ) Considerations In prescribing regulations under subparagraph ( A ), the agencies shall weigh ( i ) the benefits to consumers with the costs on furnishers and the credit reporting system ; ( ii ) the impact on the overall accuracy and integrity of consumer reports of any such requirements ; ( iii ) whether direct contact by the consumer with the furnisher would likely result in the most expeditious resolution of any such dispute ; and ( iv ) the potential impact on the credit reporting process if credit repair organizations, as defined in section 1679a ( 3 ) of this title, including entities that would be a credit repair organization, but for section 1679a ( 3 ) ( B ) ( i ) of this title, are able to circumvent the prohibition in subparagraph ( G ). ( C ) Applicability Subparagraphs ( D ) through ( G ) shall apply in any circumstance identified under the regulations promulgated under subparagraph ( A ). ( D ) Submitting a notice of dispute A consumer who seeks to dispute the accuracy of information shall provide a dispute notice directly to such person at the address specified by the person for such notices that ( i ) identifies the specific information that is being disputed ; ( ii ) explains the basis for the dispute; and ( iii ) includes all supporting documentation required by the furnisher to substantiate the basis of the dispute. ( E ) Duty of person after receiving notice of dispute After receiving a notice of dispute from a consumer pursuant to subparagraph ( D ), the person that provided the information in dispute to a consumer reporting agency shall ( i ) conduct an investigation with respect to the disputed information ; ( ii ) review all relevant information provided by the consumer with the notice ; ( iii ) complete such persons investigation of the dispute and report the results of the investigation to the consumer before the expiration of the period under section 1681i ( a ) ( 1 ) of this title within which a consumer reporting agency would be required to complete its action if the consumer had elected to dispute the information under that section; and ( iv ) if the investigation finds that the information reported was inaccurate, promptly notify each consumer reporting agency to which the person furnished the inaccurate information of that determination and provide to the agency any correction to that information that is necessary to make the information provided by the person accurate. ( F ) Frivolous or irrelevant dispute ( i ) In general This paragraph shall not apply if the person receiving a notice of a dispute from a consumer reasonably determines that the dispute is frivolous or irrelevant, including ( I ) by reason of the failure of a consumer to provide sufficient information to investigate the disputed information ; or ( II ) the submission by a consumer of a dispute that is substantially the same as a dispute previously submitted by or for the consumer, either directly to the person or through a consumer reporting agency under subsection ( b ), with respect to which the person has already performed the persons duties under this paragraph or subsection ( b ), as applicable. ( ii ) Notice of determination Upon making any determination under clause ( i ) that a dispute is frivolous or irrelevant, the person shall notify the consumer of such determination not later than 5 business days after making such determination, by mail or, if authorized by the consumer for that purpose, by any other means available to the person. ( iii ) Contents of notice A notice under clause ( ii ) shall include ( I ) the reasons for the determination under clause ( i ) ; and ( II ) identification of any information required to investigate the disputed information, which may consist of a standardized form describing the general nature of such information. ( G ) Exclusion of credit repair organizations This paragraph shall not apply if the notice of the dispute is submitted by, is prepared on behalf of the consumer by, or is submitted on a form supplied to the consumer by, a credit repair organization, as defined in section 1679a ( 3 ) of this title, or an entity that would be a credit repair organization, but for section 1679a ( 3 ) ( B ) ( i ) of this title. ( b ) Duties of furnishers of information upon notice of dispute ( 1 ) In general After receiving notice pursuant to section 1681i ( a ) ( 2 ) of this title of a dispute with regard to the completeness or accuracy of any information provided by a person to a consumer reporting agency, the person shall ( A ) conduct an investigation with respect to the disputed information ; ( B ) review all relevant information provided by the consumer reporting agency pursuant to section 1681i ( a ) ( 2 ) of this title ; ( C ) report the results of the investigation to the consumer reporting agency ; ( D ) if the investigation finds that the information is incomplete or inaccurate, report those results to all other consumer reporting agencies to which the person furnished the information and that compile and maintain files on consumers on a nationwide basis ; and ( E ) if an item of information disputed by a consumer is found to be inaccurate or incomplete or can not be verified after any reinvestigation under paragraph ( 1 ), for purposes of reporting to a consumer reporting agency only, as appropriate, based on the results of the reinvestigation promptly ( i ) modify that item of information ; ( ii ) delete that item of information ; or ( iii ) permanently block the reporting of that item of information. Subject : Defective Foreclosure, False Posting, and Failure to Provide Proof of Sale Complaint Summary I dispute the validity of the foreclosure conducted by XXXX XXXX XXXX. All substantive responses regarding this matter have been provided through counsel, XXXX XXXX XXXX, which represents XXXX XXXX XXXX. The foreclosure process is defective, unsupported by required documentation, and based on unreliable and contradictory representations. A foreclosure sale has been asserted, yet no evidence has been produced to establish that any valid sale occurred. This complaint should be reviewed in conjunction with my prior CFPB complaint, No. XXXX, as part of an ongoing pattern of foreclosure-related issues. Key Violations 1. Defective Posting of Notice of Trustees Sale The response provided through Aldridge Pite LLP relies on a posting declaration stating that the Notice of Trustees Sale was posted at the property. This is directly contradicted by independent records, as shown in Exhibit A, which includes documentation from the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX confirming : - No access request was made - No entry was logged - No posting occurred at the property Instead, the notice was placed at the community gate approximately one mile from the property, not at the property itself. This does not constitute compliant posting. Failure to properly post the notice calls into question the validity of the foreclosure process. 2. No Proof of Foreclosure Sale The response provided through Aldridge Pite LLP states that a foreclosure sale occurred on XX/XX/year>. However, the following has not been provided : - Trustees Deed Upon Sale - Identity of the purchaser - Sale price - Any recorded documentation confirming the sale A foreclosure sale can not be established without these documents. Despite multiple requests, no documentation has been produced to establish that any valid sale occurred. 3. Contradictory and Evasive Representations The response provided through Aldridge Pite LLP asserts that the foreclosure process complied with applicable law, while simultaneously stating that the response : should not be construed as a statement regarding the actions of any other entities. This is internally inconsistent. Assertions of statutory compliance necessarily depend on the actions of all parties involved in the foreclosure process. A party can not assert compliance while disclaiming responsibility for the underlying actions required to establish that compliance. 4. Improper Reliance on Third-Party Vendor The posting declaration relied upon appears to have been performed by a third-party vendor. However : - The trustee has a non-delegable duty to ensure compliance with foreclosure laws - Any inaccurate or false posting remains the responsibility of the trustee The discrepancy reflected in Exhibit A raises serious concerns regarding the accuracy and integrity of the foreclosure process. 5. Lack of Independent Trustee Verification XXXX XXXX XXXX has not provided any direct response or independent verification of the foreclosure process. All communications have been made through its counsel. This raises concerns as to whether the trustee independently verified compliance with statutory requirements, or is relying entirely on unverified third-party representations. A foreclosure can not be considered reliable where the trustee has not independently confirmed the validity of the process. Regulatory Concerns The conduct described above may constitute : - Misrepresentation of foreclosure compliance - Failure to maintain and provide accurate records - Failure to provide material documentation to the consumer - Potential unfair or deceptive acts or practices ( UDAAP ) Requested Resolution I request that XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX. and XXXX XXXX XXXX provide : 1. Definitive proof of whether a foreclosure sale actually occurred 2. A complete Trustees Deed Upon Sale ( if any exists ) 3. Identification of the purchaser and the full sale price 4. All documentation supporting the alleged posting of the Notice of Trustees Sale 5. A written explanation addressing the contradiction reflected in Exhibit A If these documents can not be produced, the foreclosure should be treated as invalid due to failure of statutory compliance. Closing Statement The foreclosure has been asserted through counsel without production of the documents necessary to establish that such a sale occurred, and while relying on a posting that is directly contradicted by independent records. A foreclosure can not be considered valid where required notice is not properly executed and the alleged sale is not substantiated by recorded documentation. This matter requires immediate investigation and corrective action. narrative: I am writing to formally address the ongoing noncompliance of your agency in relation to my identity theft report, which I previously submitted in accordance with the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ). I'd like to emphasize that I am the one submitting this complaint and there is no third party involved. Despite having sent multiple letters, your agency has repeatedly rejected my identity theft report on the grounds that it was not filed by a law enforcement agency. This decision is not in compliance with the FCRA and fails to recognize the guidance provided by identitytheft.gov as mandated by the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ). As you are aware, the FCRA at Section 605B and the guidance provided by the CFPB under identitytheft.gov clearly outline the process for filing an identity theft report. The CFPB specifically states that victims of identity theft can file a report directly through identitytheft.gov, which then becomes a valid identity theft report under the FCRA. Nowhere does the FCRA require this report to be submitted by law enforcement for it to be valid. Furthermore, under FCRA Section 617, your agency is legally required to investigate and resolve any identity theft dispute in a timely manner, and you are prohibited from deciding unilaterally what is valid or invalid when it comes to an identity theft report that has been properly filed. Your refusal to acknowledge this report based on your own standardsrather than what is set forth in federal lawis a clear violation of the FCRA. Legal Precedent : XXXX v. XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ( XXXX XXXX. XXXX ) : This case underscores the importance of proper handling of disputes related to credit reporting and emphasizes that credit reporting agencies can not disregard information simply based on their own internal policies when federal law mandates a specific process. 2.Sarver v. Experian Information Solutions , Inc. , 390 F.3d 969 ( 7th Cir. 2004 ) : This case reinforced that credit reporting agencies must follow FCRA regulations, including investigating claims of identity theft in accordance with the law, and can not arbitrarily determine what constitutes an acceptable identity theft report. 3.Henson v. Santander Consumer USA , Inc. , 2017 U.S. Dist . LEXIS 191143 ( E.D. Va. 2017 ) : This decision clarified that a credit reporting agency is obligated to accept documents submitted by the consumer, as long as they meet the legal requirements for disputing inaccurate information under the FCRA. The agency has an obligation to conduct a reasonable investigation itself. '' Cushman v. Trans Union Corp., 115 F.3d 220 ( 3rd Cir. 1997 ) These harms are measurable, preventable, and attributable to willful negligence and disregard of consumer protection law. XXXX XXXX XXXX Account Number XXXX Open Date XX/XX/XXXX Relief Requested : I am requesting that the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau take appropriate supervisory or enforcement action and require XXXX, XXXX, and TransUnion to : Immediately delete all negative items previously disputed that can not be verified with complete documentation Cease reporting unverifiable data and require original source validation for all disputes Re-review investigation procedures and prohibit reliance solely on e-OSCAR as a substitute for human reinvestigation Certify in writing that corrective actions have been taken and notify all furnishers and third-party users of the updated information

Cessation of Collection Efforts : NCS must cease all further collection activities related to this account, including any communications, reporting, or attempts to enforce the alleged debt. 4. Written Confirmation : NCS must provide written confirmation to me, via certified mail, that : ( a ) the account has been deleted from all credit reports ; ( b ) all collection efforts have ceased ; and ( c ) no further negative reporting will occur. narrative: I am submitting this detailed account to explain what happened regarding the item being reported under the name HWARFIELD, associated with account number XXXXXXXX XXXX The purpose of this statement is to fully describe the sequence of events, the issues with the reporting, the lack of proper validation, and the concerns surrounding the accuracy and fairness of the data currently appearing on my consumer credit reports. I am providing an extensive explanation so that the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau and the company involved can understand the full scope of the situation and take appropriate action. This report is being furnished about an account that I have no confirmed knowledge of, no documented history with, and no understanding of how it was created, assigned, transferred, or linked to my personal credit file. The appearance of this account took me by surprise, and it immediately raised concerns regarding whether this debt is legitimate, whether it is accurately associated with my identity, and whether the company involved has complied with the requirements of federal law in their handling of this matter. Because of these concerns, I am submitting this statement to outline everything that has occurred, how this situation has negatively impacted me, and why I am disputing the information associated with HWARFIELD under account number XXXXXXXX XXXX 1. Discovery of the Account I first became aware of the HWARFIELD account when reviewing my credit reports for accuracy. While checking the trade lines that appear under my name, I noticed that an account from HWARFIELD a name I did not recognize had been listed on my file. I had never received any letter, phone call, email, or message indicating that any such company had opened or owned an account connected to me. There was no prior notice under the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), no initial disclosure, no validation letter, no billing statements, and no indication that such a debt existed. This account appeared abruptly, without context, without explanation, and without any supporting information. It had never been presented to me in any form prior to its appearance on my credit file, which immediately raised concerns about whether this was a case of inaccurate reporting, a mistaken identity, a mixed-file issue, an assignment error, or an internal data mismatch within the company 's system. 2. Absence of Any Prior Communication Before a company furnishes derogatory information to a consumer reporting agency, federal law requires that they first attempt to make contact with the consumer and provide notice of the debt. In this case, HWARFIELD did not communicate with me in any lawful or recognizable form prior to placing this account on my credit report. I did not receive : A notice of debt A validation letter An itemized statement A breakdown of charges A notice of rights Any attempt to collect Any attempt to validate Any documentation at all This lack of communication is a critical part of what happened. At no point did HWARFIELD meet the legal obligations required of any entity seeking to collect or report a debt. Because they did not provide any documentation or communication prior to reporting, I had no opportunity to determine whether the account was accurate, whether the amount was correct, whether the debt was legitimate, or whether the account belonged to someone else entirely. 3. No Contract, No Agreement, No Acknowledgment I have never opened any account with HWARFIELD. I have never applied for any service, product, credit line, membership, program, or agreement through this company. I have never signed any contract, electronically or otherwise. I have never granted consent for them to pull my credit, extend credit, or conduct any transaction in my name. The absence of a contract is one of the main reasons I dispute this account. Without a contract, there is no lawful basis for HWARFIELD or any associated collector to assert that I owe them anything. A valid debt must be supported by : A signed agreement A record of the original transaction A documented account opening Clear terms and conditions Identification of the original creditor Proof of ownership of the debt A chain of assignments, if transferred None of this was provided to me at any point in time. 4. The Reporting Is Missing Key Data When an account is reported to the consumer reporting agencies, the information must be complete, accurate, and verifiable. In the case of the HWARFIELD account, several elements of the reporting were incomplete or questionable, including : Dates of account opening Dates of delinquency Dates of last activity Details of the original creditor Breakdown of balances Legal basis for assignment Identification information Payment history The trade line was reported without essential details that are required to determine whether it belongs to me. This lack of clarity suggests either internal errors, insufficient records, or a failure to maintain documentation as required. The reporting of incomplete or unverifiable information is a violation of the FCRA, and this is a major part of what happened with this account. 5. Verification Attempts Resulted in Automated Responses When I disputed the HWARFIELD account with the credit bureaus, expecting that the company would provide actual documentation or validation, the verification process did not produce any meaningful evidence. The responses from the bureaus amounted to automated confirmations generated through the e-OSCAR system, which is a highly automated data-matching tool rather than a real investigation. This means the company did not : Review original documents Confirm the identity match Provide evidence of ownership Provide account-level detail Provide a signed agreement Conduct a manual investigation Instead, the company furnished the same unverified data over again, repeating the same inaccurate information without engaging in a legally compliant investigation. This failure to meaningfully investigate is, in itself, a major part of what happened. 6. Identity and Matching Concerns Another important part of what happened is the possibility of : A mixed credit file A misreported account from another consumer An internal clerical or system error Incorrect or partial identifiers being matched to my name Data migration errors Improper third-party reporting Because HWARFIELD has not provided documentation proving the account belongs to me, it is entirely possible that the account is associated with another individual and was incorrectly linked to my file. The lack of supporting information and the absence of proper validation contribute to this concern. 7. No Proof of Assignment or Ownership If the account was originally created by another creditor and later assigned or sold to HWARFIELD, then federal law requires that : The company must have proof of ownership The assignment must be valid The chain of title must be clear All original documents must accompany the debt None of this has been provided. HWARFIELD has not demonstrated that : They legally own the debt The debt was assigned lawfully The chain of ownership is intact The amount reported is accurate The reporting is permissible Since no documentation exists, the appearance of this account seems to be the result of incomplete record-keeping or unverified data sharing between entities. 8. The Reporting Has Caused Harm Because of this account being reported without validation, communication, or supporting documentation, I have experienced : Lowered credit scores Difficulty obtaining credit Negative impression to lenders Emotional stress Time spent disputing inaccurate information Concerns about identity theft This reporting has caused me harm despite the complete absence of proof that I ever owed any debt to HWARFIELD. The presence of this account unvalidated, unsupported, and potentially inaccurate has created unnecessary hardship and has adversely affected multiple areas of my financial life. 9. My Right to Verification Was Ignored Under FDCPA guidelines ( if applicable ) and under general principles of fair reporting, I have a right to receive : Validation Verification Documentation Transparency Clear identification of the creditor Clear itemization of the amounts Because HWARFIELD never provided me with any such materials, I had no opportunity to review or dispute the debt before it was reported. This is a significant violation of standard consumer rights practices. This forms a major part of what happened : the company furnished negative information without fulfilling the most basic obligations to notify and validate. 10. A Meaningful Investigation Never Occurred After I reported the issue to the credit bureaus, hoping that HWARFIELD would be required to produce documentation, I discovered that the investigation was superficial. Rather than producing documentation or examining the validity of the debt, the company simply verified the account through automated data-matching systems. This type of investigation does not meet the legal standard of a reasonable investigation required under the FCRA. A meaningful investigation requires reviewing original records, not repeating internal entries. Thus, what happened is that the company failed to conduct a legitimate investigation into my dispute. 11. The Reporting Is Unverifiable, Incomplete, and Questionable Every component of the reporting for the HWARFIELD account raises questions : No documentation No communication No signed agreement No validation No proof of ownership No itemization No timeline consistency No clear connection to me This suggests that the account may not legitimately belong to me and that the reporting is based on insufficient or inaccurate records. 12. Summary of What Happened To summarize in clear terms : An account under HWARFIELD XXXXXXXX XXXX appeared on my credit report without any prior notice to me. I have no knowledge of this company and never opened an account with them. The company never contacted me, never validated the account, and never provided any documentation. The reporting is incomplete, inaccurate, and missing essential identifiers. Disputes resulted in automated verification, not real investigations. No contract, agreement, application, billing history, or chain of title has been produced. The reporting has negatively affected my financial life. Based on all available evidence, this account appears to be inaccurately reported and unverified. This concludes what happened.

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY : SPS has asserted a default by redefining amounts due using categories that do not appear in the Business Promissory Note or Mortgage. This resulted in the apparent misapplication of payments, continued assessment of default-rate interest after cure, and the creation of default-rate payment figures that do not correspond to any provision in the loan documents. SPS is demanding more than {$19000.00} in amounts that I can not reconcile to the Note or Mortgage and has issued a Notice of Default based on these figures. My XX/XX/XXXX payment exceeded all amounts then due under the Note, yet the account continued to be treated as in default. I am requesting regulatory review and correction of the account. ANALYSIS : 1. SPS redefined amounts due using categories not contained in the Note, leading to an asserted default. The Note defines the monthly amount due as the principal-and-interest installment and the applicable late fee. SPS increased the amount due by including escrow items, shortages, advances, default-rate principal and interest, and other categories that are not identified in the Note as amounts due and payable under the Note. This redefinition of amount due appears to be the upstream issue that resulted in the asserted default and the downstream payment application errors. 2. SPS applied my XX/XX/XXXX payment to non-Note items even though the payment exceeded the amount then due under the Note. On XX/XX/XXXX, I paid {$4000.00}. At that time, the amounts due under the Note consisted of the XXXX principal-and-interest installment and the applicable late fee. The payment exceeded those amounts. Section D of the Note permits discretionary application only when a payment is less than all amounts due and payable under the Note. Because my payment exceeded the amount then due under the Note, Section D was not triggered by its terms. Despite this, SPS appears to have applied funds to escrow, advances, default interest, suspense, or other non-Note items rather than fully satisfying the XXXX installment and late fee. This application resulted in the account continuing to be treated as in default even though the Note-defined obligations had been satisfied. 3. Default-rate treatment continued after the XXXX installment was cured. Section H.1 of the Note addresses default-rate interest when a monthly installment remains unpaid for 30 days or more. Once the XXXX installment and late fee were paid on XX/XX/XXXX, any basis for continuing default-rate treatment tied to that installment ceased. However, the account reflects continued default-rate treatment after XX/XX/XXXX. I have not been provided with contractual authority supporting this continued assessment. 4. SPS demanded payment figures that do not correspond to any provision in the Note or Mortgage. SPS demanded {$9800.00} and {$19000.00} as payments due as according to their letters dated XX/XX/XXXX and XXXX, respectively. I have been unable to identify any provision in the Note or Mortgage that authorizes : A redefined or default-rate principal-and-interest installment, Capitalization or rolling forward of unpaid amounts into a new installment amount, or Creation of lump-sum payment figures not derived from the contractual installment structure. Section H.2 applies only after maturity or valid acceleration, neither of which had occurred at the time of the demand. The demanded figures do not correspond to the installment amounts defined in the Note. 5. Notice of Default based on amounts not derived from the loan documents. The XX/XX/XXXX Notice of Default demands a lump-sum figure that does not correspond to the installment amounts defined in the Note and includes categories that I can not reconcile to any provision in the loan documents. Because the asserted default appears to be based on non-Note categories and payment application decisions described above, there is a risk of wrongful acceleration if the account is not corrected. * * a PDF version of this complaint is attached to facilitate readability * *

I have a VA-backed mortgage with Freedom Mortgage. I requested hardship assistance during the government shutdown and was placed into a forbearance plan. Since then, I have received conflicting, confusing information from multiple representatives, and I have not been able to get clear written guidance about my delinquency status, credit impact, repayment options, or how my missed payments will be handled. When I first contacted Freedom Mortgage at the beginning of the shutdown to request hardship help, the representative asked a few questions and told me I would receive results soon. I was not told verbally that I would be considered delinquent or that my credit could be impacted. Nor did they send me any written documentation to sign. When I received the written forbearance letter, it stated that I will become delinquent and that my credit score may be impacted. It also stated that the forbearance was processed as an incomplete loss mitigation application, and that I could complete the application at any time. None of this information was explained to me before I agreed to the plan. I have attached attached the forbearance letter I received, which contains statements that conflict with the verbal information I was given. It stated the following : - My forbearance request was approved and processed as an " incomplete loss mitigation application. '' - It stated that during the forbearance period, I " will become delinquent '' on monthly payments. - It also stated that my credit score " may be impacted '' during the forbearance. - The letter explained that I " may submit a complete loss mitigation application at any time, despite being placed into the forbearance plan. '' - The letter did not explain what repayment or home-retention options would be available after the forbearance period ends, nor how missed payments would be handled. Because the letter contradicted what I thought the plan was, I called Freedom Mortgage mid XXXX to ask for clarification. On that call, I was told that my account was paused, that I was not considered delinquent, and that my credit would not be affected. I was also told to call back on XX/XX/XXXX if I needed an extension. I relied on these verbal statements because this is my first time using forbearance. However, when I called back on XX/XX/XXXX, I was told something completely different : That I owed approximately two months of payments That my account was showing as delinquent That because my loan is VA-backed, missed payments could not be moved to the end and that no payment deferral option exists. Because I received conflicting answers, I asked to be reviewed for repayment or home retention options. I was told I could not be reviewed unless I first exited the forbearance plan, which would leave me without any clear next steps. I expressed that I was uncomfortable exiting forbearance without knowing what repayment options I would have, and that this felt risky. I referenced my forbearance letter which said I could submit loss mitigation during the plan, but I was told that this was technically complete and that the representative could not offer options until after I exit. On todays call ( XX/XX/XXXX ), I was informed that : My extension request is in request mode, not review Once it enters review, my current forbearance will automatically end The new extension may not start immediately after XX/XX/XXXX There could be a gap, but no written explanation could be provided They could not guarantee how this gap might affect my account or credit They could not provide a list of repayment or modification options They could not explain in writing what will happen to my missed payments They could not provide written notes from the call They could send a custom letter, but it may not reflect what was discussed and is not guaranteed that I am approved to receive a " custom letter. '' I was also told they did not have it in writing that states the VA guidelines does not have payment deferrals and that I would have to look it up myself. I asked them to give me in writing everything they are stating to me and they said they could not provide that. This makes me lose trust and confidence of Freedom Mortgage handling my mortgage loan. Because each representative has given me different information, including contradictory statements about delinquency, credit reporting, whether exiting forbearance is required, whether repayment deferral exists, and how transitions between forbearance periods are handled, I have no clear understanding of what to expect. I am requesting CFPB assistance to help me obtain : 1. A clear written explanation of my current account status 2. Written clarification about delinquency and credit reporting 3. Written details on how my forbearance extension will be processed 4. Information on how any administrative gap between plans is handled 5. A clear list of repayment or modification options that will be available 6. Written guidance on how missed payments will be handled 7. Confirmation of the process for reviewing repayment options 8. Consistent communication that matches the written documents I receive I am simply trying to understand how my VA loan is being handled, how my hardship assistance works, and what repayment options will be available afterward. Because of the inconsistent information I have received from multiple representatives, I am asking for CFPB help so that everything can be clarified in writing.
