narrative: This complaint concerns the continued reporting and verification of the Chapter XXXX bankruptcy identified as Ref : XXXX, which appears in the public records section of my consumer credit reports. The purpose of this complaint is to document the inaccuracies, verification failures, and unlawful reporting practices surrounding this bankruptcy record, and to request that the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau intervene to ensure compliance with the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ). I am not disputing the historical fact that a Chapter XXXX case maXXXX have existed. Instead, I am disputing the accuracy, verification, source, timing, and procedural compliance of how this particular bankruptcy record is appearing on my credit reports. Because the credit bureaus failed to verify the information with the original bankruptcy court, relied on unauthorized third-party vendors, and refused to provide the required method-of-verification documentation during reinvestigation, the reporting of this record violates multiple provisions of federal law. This narrative provides a complete, detailed, and lawful description of what occurred and why this bankruptcy is being reported improperly. XXXX. How I Discovered the Reporting Problem While reviewing my credit reports, I noticed that a Chapter XXXX bankruptcy labeled Ref : XXXX was XXXX. Immediately, issues were apparent : The date formatting was unusual and did not resemble standard federal bankruptcy docket formatting. The reference number included codes ( XXXX ) that did not match official U.S. court documentation. Different credit bureaus displayed the record differently. Details such as the court location, chapter, docket number, and disposition were incomplete. The status of the case was inconsistent across bureaus. Because bankruptcy information must be precise and match the official court record, these irregularities raised questions about whether the listing was accurate, up-to-date, or verified properly. 2. Bankruptcy Courts Do NOT Furnish or Verify Information for Credit Reports One of the most important facts is this : Federal bankruptcy courts do not : Furnish consumer data to credit bureaus Verify bankruptcy information for private companies Communicate with credit bureaus during reinvestigation Participate in consumer reporting Authorize third-party vendors to transmit bankruptcy records This means that any claim by a credit bureau that this bankruptcy was verified did not come from the court. Instead, the verification originated from third-party public-record vendors, which are not original, legal sources of bankruptcy information. 3. The Reporting Uses a Non-Court Reference Number A true bankruptcy reference must match the official docket format, such as XXXX XXXX XXXX District identifiers ( XXXX, MO-W ) However, the reference XXXX is not consistent with : PACER docket formatting CM/ECF XXXX XXXX Bankruptcy Court indexing Clerk of Court dispositions Standard case numbering found in federal filings This strongly suggests the information is not based on court records but on automated OCR scraping or vendor indexing, which is prone to errors. 4. I Filed Disputes with All Three Bureaus Upon discovering inconsistencies, I exercised my rights under FCRA 611 ( a ) and disputed the bankruptcy with all three major bureaus. In each dispute, I requested : The method of verification Identification of the source of the information Copies of any documents reviewed The name of the furnisher A detailed description of procedures used The public record as obtained from the court These are rights guaranteed under FCRA 609 and 611. 5. Bureaus Returned Generic Verified as Accurate Responses All bureaus responded with nearly identical automated letters stating that the bankruptcy had been verified and would remain. However : No bureau provided the method of verification No bureau named a furnisher No documentation was provided No court records were shown No detailed procedures were disclosed No evidence was produced showing original record review This confirms that : The reinvestigation was automated, not meaningful. 6. The Reinvestigation Was Unreasonable The FCRA requires a reasonable reinvestigation. For a public record like bankruptcy, reasonableness requires : Reviewing the original docket Confirming filing and dismissal dates Verifying the case disposition Matching the reference number Confirming the bankruptcy chapter Ensuring reporting matches the official court record But the bureaus did : No contact with the XXXX Bankruptcy XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX No comparison to official documents No document examination No human involvement Instead, they relied solely on automated responses from a vendor such as XXXX or another public-record scraper. 7. Third-Party Vendors Are NOT an Acceptable Source XXXX XXXX XXXX FCRA XXXX FCRA requires thaXXXX public records be verified using accurate, reliable, court-sourced information. However, credit bureaus rely on : XXXX XXXX CoreLogic Data-harvesting companies Public-record scrapers Automated XXXX systems These companies : Are not original sources Do not certify accuracy Do not verify XXXX data Are prone to errors Are not authorized by courts Because this bankruptcy record depends entirely on third-party vendor data, it can not be considered verified. XXXX. Inconsistencies Across Bureaus Prove the Data Is Inaccurate For a bankruptcy to be accurate, all bureaus must report : The same dates The same reference The same court location The same status The same disposition However, the reporting for XXXX contains significant inconsistencies : Dates differ across bureaus Status ( dismissed versus open versus verified ) varies Reference numbers differ Update timestamps do not match Case details differ Under FCRA 607 ( b ), bureaus must ensure maximum possible accuracy. The inconsistencies demonstrate non-compliance. 9. Bankruptcy Reporting Windows May Be Incorrect A Chapter 13 bankruptcy may remain on a credit report for : 7 years from the date of filing, not dismissal. If the XXXX portion of the reference corresponds to XX/XX/year>, then : The record may have been misdated The filing date XXXX not match court records The dismissal/verification date ( XXXX ) XXXX not be legally relevant If the wrong date is used, the bankruptcy may already be : Outside the legal reporting window Reported for too long Reported prematurely Reported with incorrect dates All of this violates the FCRA. 10. Failure to Provide the Method of Verification Under FCRA 611 ( a ) ( 6 ) ( B ) ( iii ), when a consumer asks how an entry was verified, the bureau must provide : The method The procedures The documentation The source of the information None of the bureaus complied. This failure alone makes the bankruptcy legally unverifiable, requiring deletion under 611 ( a ) ( 5 ) ( A ). 11. The Bankruptcy Record Was Not Verified Using the Original Court Docket I obtained official bankruptcy documents from the federal court system and compared them to the reporting. Those documents included : The petition filing The docket sheet Case disposition XXXX XXXX XXXX notices Dismissal order These official documents do not match the way the credit bureaus report the record. The formatting, numbers, and dates differ. This proves the bureaus did not review : PACER documents CM/ECF filings XXXX of XXXX XXXX XXXX, the verification is illegitimate. 12. The Reporting Is Incomplete and Misleading For bankruptcy, bureaus must report : Correct filing date Correct status Correct docket number Correct court Correct chapter Correct disposition Accurate timestamps However, the entry labeled XXXX is XXXX Incomplete Misformatted Not court-standard Missing the precise court identifier Missing core docket information Not identical to official records Incomplete public records violate the FCRAs accuracy mandate. 13. The Bankruptcy May Have Been Reported Based on a Misindexed Case Third-party vendors often : Misread docket entries Pull incomplete data Merge unrelated cases Apply non-court reference numbers Assign internal indexing codes Misrepresent dates The XXXX reference XXXX suggests : A vendor indexing code Not an actual bankruptcy court file Therefore, the reporting is likely based on : Misindexed data A misread case Inaccurate vendor interpretation Credit bureaus can not legally maintain vendor-generated errors. XXXX. Harm Caused by the Improper Reporting The inaccurate and unverifiable reporting of this bankruptcy has caused : Lower credit scores Higher interest rates Denied credit applications Loss of financial opportunities Difficulty obtaining housing Employment barriers Insurance impacts Emotional distress Difficulty rebuilding credit A bankruptcy is one of the most damaging items on a credit report. When reported inaccurately, the harm is compounded. 15. The Bureaus Violated Multiple FCRA Sections The reporting of this bankruptcy violates : 607 ( b ) Accuracy requirement 611 ( a ) Failure to reinvestigate reasonably 611 ( a ) ( 6 ) ( B ) ( iii ) Failure to provide method of verification 611 ( a ) ( 5 ) Failure to delete unverifiable information 609 ( a ) ( 1 ) Failure to provide the source of information 623 Furnisher accuracy obligations The bankruptcy is therefore unlawfully reported. Conclusion The Chapter XXXX bankruptcy Ref : XXXX is XXXX reported inaccurately, without proper verification, using unauthorized third-party vendor data, and without adherence to FCRA procedures. The credit bureaus did not verify the information with the bankruptcy court, did not provide method-of-verification details, did not review original court documents, and did not maintain maximum possible accuracy. Because the bankruptcy is unverified, inaccurate, incomplete, and improperly sourced, it is unlawful for it to remain on my credit file. I request immediate CFPB intervention to ensure that the credit bureaus comply with federal law.

I am submitting this formal complaint regarding my mortgage servicers failure to timely endorse and return an insurance claim check, resulting in unnecessary delays in essential home repairs and financial hardship. Per standard procedure, I promptly forwarded the check to the servicer for endorsement so I could pay contractors and move forward with repairs. To my dismay, the mortgage servicer has failed to act within a reasonable timeframe. When I contacted the customer service line, I was connected with an outsourced call center that provided minimal assistance and a generic processing timeline of XXXX business days, followed by an additional 5 days for return via standard USPS. These representatives were unable to provide clear status updates or escalate the issue despite the fact that the repairs have already begun and time is of the essence. I can see on my mortgage account that the funds are available ; however, Freedom refuses to grant me the funds and says I have to wait another XXXX days. I asked about the company receiving interests on the funds and the customer service person indicated they do, but I will not get that funding. To illustrate the disparity in service : another financial institution, which was also listed on the check as a lienholder, was able to endorse and return the check within 30 minutes of receipt. This highlights that the excessive delay on the part of Freedom Mortgage is not industry standard but rather a reflection of inefficient and unresponsive business practices. Concerns : Unreasonable Delay : The processing timeframe is excessive and not reflective of current technological or industry capabilities. Lack of Communication and Transparency : Customer service provided no substantive updates, refused to expedite the process, and failed to provide confirmation of receipt or expected completion date. Outsourced Call Center Deficiencies : The thir d-party representatives were unable to address or escalate urgent homeowner issues. This lack of empowerment and training puts consumers at further risk. Financial Harm and Risk to Property : Due to the delay, I am facing delays in payment to contractors, which jeopardizes ongoing repair work and could increase costs. Potential UDAAP Violation : The servicer 's actions may constitute an unfair or abusive practice under the CFPBs standards due to the failure to process critical claim funds in a timely and transparent manner. Requested Action : I request the CFPB investigate this matter and require Freedom Mortgage to : Immediately process and return my endorsed check via overnight mail ; Review and reform their insurance claims processing policies to reflect reasonable turnaround times ; Improve transparency by providing timely status updates and points of contact for urgent matters ; Ensure customer service representatives are adequately trained and equipped to handle time-sensitive claims. I am seeking relief not only for myself but also to prevent other homeowners from experiencing similar treatment during a time of distress. Mortgage servicers should not be allowed to delay disbursement of insurance proceeds with no accountability. Thank you for your attention to this matter.

issue: Attempts to collect debt not owed
narrative: XXXX XXXX. XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, NY XXXX Trans Union XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX, PA XXXX To Whom it may concern, I am writing to formally dispute inaccurate information being reported on my credit report regarding a charge-off. The accounts in question are listed as follows : Creditor Name : XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX Account # : XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX Date of Charge-Off : XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX It has come to my attention that the charge-off is being reported month after month on my payment history, which is incorrect. According to the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), negative information such as a charge-off should only be reported once, corresponding to the date it was charged off. The FCRA requires that credit reporting agencies ensure the accuracy of the information they report ( 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ) ). Repeatedly reporting the monthly charge-off results in a misleading and inaccurate credit report, which has significantly harmed my credit score. Additionally, the statute of limitations for reporting a charge-off is seven years from the date of the first delinquency that led to the charge-off ( 15 U.S.C. 1681c ( a ) ( 4 ) ). Continuously reporting this charge-off as a new event each month does not reset the statute of limitations and is improper. I request that you promptly investigate this account and correct the inaccurate information by removing the repeated entries of the charge-off from my payment history. Please update my credit report accordingly and confirm these corrections for me. Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter. Sincerely, XXXX XXXX. XXXX

Experian, acting as a federally regulated data broker and credit reporting agency, can not use its system of influence to penalize or intimidate consumers for invoking their legal rights. I strongly believe that I have been targeted in retaliation for exercising my federally protected rights under the FCRA, and this act constitutes not only unprofessionalism, but potentially abusive and coercive behavior in violation of broader consumer protection statutes under 15 U.S. Code 45 ( FTC Act Unfair and Deceptive Practices ). ________________________________________ Thank you for your time and attention to this matter. Misuse of Government Assistance : The improper treatment of the DPA loan as a collectible debt, without providing required documentation, raises concerns about the improper conversion of government assistance into private enforceable debt. This could violate federal and state guidelines governing the disbursement and management of housing assistance programs. Harm Caused Due to these actions, I have faced the following harm : Collection Activity on a Disputed Debt : The company has initiated collection activities on a loan that is disputed, potentially unenforceable, and improperly documented. I have to date, received no proof that I owe your company any debt and I am requesting that you forward to me full and proper documentation as evidence of this alleged debt. As per the FDCPA, it is a violation for any debt collector to pursue collection activity on an account without notifying the debtor in writing within 5 days after any communication. Additionally I am allowed 30 days to dispute the validity of the debt. If you are unable to provide me with proper proof then you must stop attempting to collect this alleged debt. If you continue to claim I owe a debt that you can not confirm with proof then you will be in direct violation of the FDCPA. Additionally, any attempt on your part to report this alleged debt to my credit reports will be a violation of the Fair Credit Reporting Act. Please forward your documentation to me upon receipt of this certified letter. Please note that proper documentation is not a print out or bill from you but rather actual proof of the debt & # 39 ; s existence which should include : -The name and address of the original creditor. -A detailed account of the alleged debt, including the amount owed and the nature of the debt specifically the services provided. -Verification or a copy of any documents that demonstrate my agreement to pay this debt, specifically a contract bearing my signature. -Proof that your company is licensed to collect debts in my state. - Proof that your company has been assigned the right to collect this debt on behalf of the original creditor, including an agreement that states that I would be liable to pay someone other than the original creditor. Regarding the last point, it is essential for you to demonstrate that you have the legal authority to collect this debt on behalf of the original creditor. Dear Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ), I am writing to formally lodge a complaint against XXXX, XXXX, and Experian for numerous violations of the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), specifically regarding their failure to comply with 15 U.S.C. 1681a ( 2 ) ( A ) ( i ) and 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 regarding the accuracy of information reported to consumer reporting agencies. Background As a consumer impacted by the actions of these credit reporting agencies, I have painstakingly attempted to correct inaccuracies in my credit report and have witnessed firsthand the failure of these agencies to adhere to statutory obligations under the FCRA. Violations 1. Definition of Consumer Report ( 15 U.S.C. 1681a ( 2 ) ( A ) ( i ) ) : It is my understanding that according to this regulation, a consumer report does not include information solely related to transactions and experiences between the consumer and the entity making the report. However, I have found that inaccuracies concerning my transactional history have been reported by these agencies, despite these inaccuracies not being exempt reports. This misclassification directly violates the clear stipulation outlined in the FCRA. 2. Responsibilities of Furnishers of Information ( 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ) : According to subsection ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ), furnishers of information have a duty to provide accurate information. I have documented occasions where both XXXX and XXXX have reported false information while having actual knowledge of errors. These inaccuracies have negatively impacted my credit score and my ability to obtain credit. Such actions are not only illegal but demonstrate a willful disregard for the law. 3. In my opinion and preliminary calculations, my home 's value should easily surpass the 80 % LTV minimum required to eliminate PMI. I contacted Mr. Cooper in XX/XX/XXXX to request that my PMI be removed in light of the improvements that I made to the property. I was first told by the PMI department that they will need to submit in writing the improvements and amounts spent to XXXX XXXX in order to have PMI removed. I am told that since the amounts are so close, I shouldnt need to complete any appraisals but that they will check into it and call me back. No one called me back. I followed up two weeks later and this time I was told that the original agent did not outline the improvements in specific-enough terminology. I reviewed the amounts/dates again with the new agent and was told they would submit and get back to me. No one calls me back. It is now XX/XX/XXXX when I contact Mr. Cooper again. This time a new agent apologizes for the false information I was previously given. I spend over an hour on the phone with her, again outlining the situation and the dates/amounts of the improvements. The new agent indicates I will need to have an informal appraisal completed. This would mean that someone would come to the house and walk around the exterior. I would not need to be home and the person would not need to see inside of the home. This would not cost me any money. I agreed to this process and she submitted that request. I am told someone will call me within 30 days with further information. After 30 days and no one calling me, I again contact Mr Cooper in XXXX XXXX. At this point, I am told that ALL of the previous agents were incorrect. Because my loan is less than one year old, I would need to obtain and pay for a complete formal appraisal which would run ballpark of {$500.00}. They can not explain why I was given false information, nor why I was never contacted about the previous requests that were submitted. I agree to the formal appraisal and Mr Cooper says they will expedite the request. I am contacted by the appraiser ( XXXX. ) and we set date for XX/XX/XXXX. XXXX. comes to my home and takes pictures/measurements of all of the rooms and exterior. He asks about improvements we have made. He says we should get the results of the appraisal in a week or two from the bank. We arent sure who he means by the bank but assume it will work itself out. I contact Mr Cooper one week later for an update they havent received the appraisal report from XXXX. I contact Mr. Cooper again at the two week, three week, and four week marks each time I am told that they havent received the appraisal report from XXXX. As it was then a month since the appraisal, I contacted XXXX. directly to inquire about the status of the report. He tells me that roughly one week after the appraisal, he received a cancellation from the bank and was told not to proceed with the report. XXXX. told me that he had a question in regards to a Maintenance Agreement. ( My home is roughly 1.5 miles back a private legal right-of-way which is in the deed. There is no Maintenance Agreement as it is a deeded right-of-way. We do not live in a neighborhood with HOA, etc. which would necessitate a Maintenance Agreement and I have never heard of this before. ) XXXX. tells me that he contacted the bank to inquire how he should proceed with valuing the property with this scenario, and the bank told him to cancel the entire appraisal. I immediately call Mr. Cooper and relay the same information. I am told they have no record of the appraisal being canceled, and they are still waiting on the report. After explaining everything multiple times to different reps, they finally agree to submit a request to XXXX XXXX for an update. I go back-and-forth with Mr Cooper over the course of the next two weeks and spend many hours on the phone with different agents. Eventually I am told that XXXX XXXX responded - the appraisal was canceled due to Lack of Access to the property. They have no idea why seeing as XXXX. accessed my property and even took pictures. They submit more requests to XXXX XXXX to hopefully salvage the appraisal since XXXX. already had most of the report finished. At this point I even tried to contact XXXX XXXX directly and was told they cant help borrowers directly and I need to contact my loan servicer. Over the past one week, I was told that Mr Cooper agents were submitting a Voice of the Customer type of complaint to escalate my problem to management. On XX/XX/XXXX, I receive an email from a new company called XXXX inviting me to schedule an appraisal with a different appraiser entirely ( XXXX. ). Their website is malfunctioning, so I google the company XXXX. directly. This company has a slew of complaints from previous customers for various reasons such as poor customer service, lack of communication, timeliness issues, and even grossly undervalued appraisals compared to local comps. Again I contact Mr. Cooper for clarification the agent doesnt know anything about any new appraisals. They still dont have any updates from management, and they are still hoping to salvage the previous partial appraisal. I communicate my discomfort with the new assigned appraiser XXXX. On XX/XX/XXXX, I receive a call from a Team Lead at Mr. Cooper who relays that I need to schedule a brand new appraisal with XXXX. I again explain the problem and my concerns regarding XXXX, inquiring why I cant use previously assigned appraiser XXXX. The Team Lead agent tells me she doesnt know, but she will again document my concerns and escalate. As of today, I still do not have any resolution to why- or how long- I will continue to pay PMI despite the value of my home being satisfactory for cancellation. Further, the loan is now over one year old which means that according to Mr. Cooper 's original statement, the PMI should simply be removed based on description/values of improvements made to the property and no formal appraisal should be required. It has been approximately 4.5 months since I initially requested for my PMI to be removed from my loan. I have spent roughly {$420.00} in PMI premiums during that same time period for which I do not feel that I am liable. On top of this, I must take off another day of work to accommodate a brand new appraisal, which I am told will cost upwards of {$500.00} and will take another month to complete start-to-finish with an appraisal company XXXX. that I am not comfortable with. From the beginning of my write up, please remember that my original ballpark LTV ratio was 81.79 %. All of the above phone calls ( XXXX total hours ) I have spent on the phone with Mr. Cooper over the last 4.5 months are in regards to the value of my home increasing by less than a mere 2 %- when I have spent upwards of {$60000.00} in improvements to the property. Mr. Cooper and/or XXXX XXXX have failed to follow the requirements set forth in The Homeowner 's Protection Act of 1998 for timely removal of PMI within 30 days of the homeowners request.

I got into contract in XX/XX/2023 to purchase an investment property, and locked in a mortgage rate a few days later with " CalCon Mutual Mortgage LLC dba OneTrust Home Loans '', led by XXXX XXXX as the Loan Originator. Leading up to the rate lock-in, I was provided confusing, mixed information about seller credits, where I was told by the Sales Manager that I could likely get my closing costs covered completely by the seller by increasing the purchase price to offset the seller 's credit. This sounded great, as I was hoping to put all the cash towards at 25 % + down payment only, while having the seller cover all the one-time closing costs. After a few days already being in contract, I found out that the original loan estimates and seller credits were not feasible, as there is a 2 % cap on seller 's credit for investment properties. Yes, I could have done more research coming in to know such a cap existed, but I was explicitly advised to make an offer that was not possible. The other nebulous action that this team took right from our first conversation, was providing enticing rates below 6 %, even though the PAR rate was above 7 % for investment properties at the time. As a less experienced investor, they did not explain that there were large point buy-downs built in right from the start. I ( somewhat naively ) asked the Sales Manager how they were able to provide a rate so much lower than the other lender I was considering, to which they said, " To be honest, I don't really care what other lenders are offering. We know we offer the best. '' This is not an exact quote, and I do not have proof of this, so I understand it carries little weight. But I do remember that moment vividly, as it reflected the salesperson 's quick and frank confidence. My other lender that I nearly selected did not mention the seemingly unlimited seller credits, nor did he start our conversation with the heavily bought-down interest rate. In retrospect, I now know that the other lender was not skipping any steps to get me to the right decision, and would have been the more prudent choice to step through each decision with. I understand I could have walked away at any moment, but I had committed in my mind to securing the purchase of this property, so it would be difficult to back out at this time and start over. With this background in mind, when my offer was accepted, it included {$20000.00} in seller 's credits, which was more than double the 2 % maximum for this investment property. Yet somehow, for the next month as we worked through inspection and repair negotiations, revised closing documents continued to have this {$20000.00} appear in closing disclosures, or other over-inflated credit amounts that were clearly above 2 %. I had asked them on multiple occasions if they would be willing to cover some of the costs as a courtesy, due to the multiple errors I'd faced. They said they would, but it was done in a very nebulous way that was not clearly itemized. Therefore, I thought that the over-inflated seller credit amount itemized in loan estimates was actually just showing that the lender had combined some of their credits with the seller credits that I'd originally been promised, as a courtesy for the mistake. However, it turned out that that all the over-inflated seller credits were true errors, and not the lender 's attempting to provide courtesy coverage of costs. I repeatedly asked if they could provide a straight forward, itemized lender 's credit, or cover my appraisal fee in some way. No one could give me a straight answer for days, until finally the VP of Lending called me and explained that the 2 % cap applies to all parties, not just the seller credit. So finally it was clear why they could not provide a courtesy lender credit, after multiple days were lost in back and forth confusion and incorrect documents. Up until nearly a month into the process, they were still providing disclosures with overinflated seller 's credits. We were working with a slower-moving corporate i-Buyer as the seller, and so having to correct the offer and clarify loan estimates likely costed us days in negotiations with the seller. While this team was not the only reason the escrow period took longer than anyone expected, the ambiguity in their terms and mistakes made in their processing ultimately costed me time, and money. This brings me to the final point of this complaint. The lock-in agreement that I signed, had no mention of the fees that would be incurred with lock-in rate extensions. Yet, as the lock-in rate was nearing its expiration, the only person that mentioned the expiration was my realtor. No one from the lending team reminded me that the rate was expiring soon, nor did they notify me that I was being charged daily fees once the rate did ultimately expire, and needed to be " extended ''. Extensions are commonplace in real estate, and no where did it mention that " extension '' meant " daily extension fees ''. After I'd already been quietly charged 2 days worth of extension fees, the team finally contacted me via text near close of business on Friday, asking if I could sign closing documents via a notary that very evening, in order to prevent further extension fees. This left me no time to organize the signing, so I worked with Title to schedule a Saturday signing. Then, the lenders informed the Title company that they would need to redraw documents ( without telling me ), in order to add the next day 's extension fees to the the closing costs. However, the team did not make the time to redraw the documents before Saturday, so we instead had to push the notary signing until Monday, adding 3 extra days of daily extension fees, despite my readiness to sign on Saturday. Due to this delayed signing that was out of my hands, I asked if they would cover the daily extension fees as a courtesy for those days, to which they very directly declined to do so, with no rationale. Then, when I probed for a reason, they blamed the lock-in rate expiration on my repair negotiation delays, and felt no reason to cover the fees as a courtesy, taking no responsibility for at least a portion of the delays. To be clear, I do not expect them to cover all the extension fees, just the days of Saturday, Sunday, and Monday, since those 3 extra days were added even though I had agreed to sign sooner. At this point, it was clear they were irritated with my request, as I'd asked for courtesy multiple times throughout the escrow period. However being irritated with a client should not rationalize burdening the client with undue financial costs. Ultimately, this entire lending experience bordered on negligence, as almost all communication after the initial sales pitch, I had to initiate contact and request corrections, or clarification of what I was looking at. This team works fast, which may seem good at the surface to get the deal, but too fast may lead to errors and neglect.

Furthermore, under the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ) 1692e ( 8 ), a debt collector is prohibited from communicating or reporting credit information they know or should know to be false. Reporting a debt tied to the wrong name and address is misleading and violates this section. Because this account does not belong to me and is tied to an address that is not mine, it appears to be either fraudulent or the result of identity theft. Under FCRA 605B, once a consumer notifies the bureaus of identity theft, the account must be blocked from their credit reports within four business days. I am requesting the immediate permanent removal of this rental collection account from all of my credit reports ( Experian, Equifax, and TransUnion ). I am also requesting that the collection agency be required to cease reporting this inaccurate account, as it is in violation of both the FCRA and FDCPA.

This letter expresses dissatisfaction with the banking institutions new policy requiring cellphones for all online banking logins. This new requirement hinders the ability to access and manage bank accounts conveniently and efficiently. This policy presents several accessibility and practicality challenges : Accessibility Concerns : Many individuals, including seniors, those with disabilities, or those who choose not to own a smartphone, rely on alternative methods for accessing online services. This new policy creates a barrier to accessing accounts and potentially excludes a significant portion of the customer base. Privacy Concerns : Linking a personal cellphone to financial accounts raises privacy concerns, particularly regarding data security and the potential for unauthorized access if the device is lost or compromised. Dependency on Technology : Requiring a cellphone at all times to access accounts, is unrealistic, and creates an undue dependency on a single piece of technology, leading to potential disruptions in service or personal inconvenience if the phone is lost, damaged, or out of battery. I have contacted the various banking institutions that I use, and I have requested a PIN be used as a secondary means of authentication. 1st- Username, 2nd- Password, 3rd- would be a PIN that only the user would know. I believe a viable alternative to the mandatory use of a cellphone for online banking logins would be a PIN that only the user would know. Other possible alternatives I would like : * * A PIN, used after the username and password is entered, that only the customer knows. * * 1st- Username, 2nd- Password, 3rd- would be a PIN that only the user would know * Hardware Security Keys ( e.g., XXXX ) This will only work on a desktop. Email-based One-Time Passwords ( OTP ) ( This still isnt realistic if your phone is lost or stolen, especially if traveling outside the country, and /or using an alternative device that isnt the owner of the bank account. ) Options for landline phone calls for authentication. ( Though this still isnt realistic if your phone is lost or stolen especially if traveling outside the United States ) These policies that are being used at nearly every financial institution is unacceptable and negatively impacts the banking experience. I believe this new option will provide customers with more flexibility in accessing their online accounts in the event of an emergency and not having access to your personal cellphone or a personal device in which to login from. I request a mandatory requirement that will provide customers with more flexibility in accessing their online accounts without having to use an additional device.

narrative: CFPB Case No. : XXXX Creditor : Synchrony Bank Account : XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX I am resubmitting this complaint to dispute Synchrony Banks response and fraud claim denial, which misstates my position, ignores material evidence, and fails to demonstrate a lawful investigation. At no time have I denied ownership of this account. As clearly stated in my police report and all prior submissions, the Verizon Visa account was opened in my name. My dispute has never concerned account ownership. My dispute is that I did not provide consent for the disputed transactions, nor did I authorize, participate in, or benefit from them. The transactions at issue resulted from unauthorized use of my card by another individual, as documented in my police report. 1. Failure to Establish Cardholder Consent Synchrony asserts that I authorized, participated in, or benefited from the purchases, yet provides no evidence that I provided consent for any transaction. To date, Synchrony has not produced : Any signed or recorded authorization Any written or electronic consent from me Any evidence showing my agreement to the purchases Any proof that I personally received or benefited from the transactions Consent is the controlling issue, not mere account ownership or card presence. Absent proof of my consent, these transactions can not be deemed authorized. 2. Improper Reliance on Card-Present Transactions Synchrony relies on the assertion that the card was physically present at the point of sale. This reasoning is legally insufficient. Card-present activity does not establish cardholder authorization and does not substitute for consent. A card can be used by another individual without the cardholders permission. Synchronys position improperly conflates physical possession of a card with lawful authorization by the account holder. 3. Complete Disregard of Police Report Evidence I submitted a police report as part of my fraud claim and CFPB complaint. That report documents : Unauthorized use of my card Lack of consent for the disputed transactions The identity and conduct of the individual responsible Synchronys response does not address this report at all. There is no analysis, rebuttal, or explanation for disregarding it. Ignoring sworn law-enforcement documentation is inconsistent with a reasonable investigation. 4. Failure to Conduct a Reasonable Investigation By denying my claim without establishing consent, disregarding my police report, and relying solely on unsupported assumptions, Synchrony failed to conduct a reasonable investigation. A lawful investigation requires : Evaluation of submitted evidence Consideration of cardholder consent Documentation supporting conclusions None of these standards were met. 5. Improper Charge-Off and Reporting During Active Dispute Despite unresolved factual disputes and a pending CFPB complaint, Synchrony charged off the account and furnished adverse credit information. This action has caused ongoing harm and was taken without a substantiated investigation.

This is what prompted my request to have a debt validation done via email. In the U.S., it is illegal for debt collectors to falsely claim they are attorneys when they are not. This is covered under the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), specifically : 15 U.S. Code 1692e False or misleading representations This section prohibits debt collectors from using any false, deceptive, or misleading representation, including : Claiming to be an attorney when they are not ( 1692e ( 3 ) ). Threatening legal action they can not or do not intend to take ( 1692e ( 5 ) ). Instead of proper validation, I received a email from XXXX XXXX, that merely states a balance and a settlement offer, which does not constitute legal validation under the FDCPA. Without sufficient documentation proving the validity of this debt, I do not acknowledge its legitimacy and continue to dispute it in its entirety. XX/XX/year>, I mailed dispute letter, including cease and desist demand. After several attempts of delivery, it was returned to me as undeliverable from address that was previously given to me the day before. Under 15 U.S.C. 1692g ( b ), a debt collector must provide adequate validation of a debt when requested, which includes : 1.The name and address of the original credito 2. A copy of the signed agreement or contract. 3. A detailed itemized accounting of how the balance was calculated. ( Any interest, fees, and complete history of payment ). 4. Verification that your company has the legal authority to collect this debt in my state. ( provide state license number, name on license, & if out of state the license for your state ). 5. Chain of assignment agreement. 6. Provide Forward Flow Agreement 7. Provide if any insurance claims have been applied or filed to this debt 8. Date of first delinquency The failure to provide a reliable mailing address for consumer disputes violates 15 U.S.C. 1692c ( c ), as it prevents me from enforcing my right to demand that your company cease further collection efforts. I request that you provide a valid address where I can send my dispute and cease communication request. This promise was false and misleading. The company shut down without honoring this advertised benefit, leaving me with no recourse, despite paying under the belief that this protection would be available. This constitutes a clear violation of 15 U.S.C. 45 ( a ) ( 1 ) of the Federal Trade Commission Act, which prohibits deceptive business practices, including false advertising and misrepresentations of service guarantees. Furthermore, XXXX never provided me with any documentation in advance identifying where in the contract this so-called Lifetime Guarantee could be voided. My treatment was not completed, yet the company and its collection agents continue to pursue me as if services were fully rendered. Adding to the deception, the contract itself was not even provided to me until after my credit had already been hit with a derogatory collection markan action that demonstrates bad faith and violates both consumer protection laws and fair credit reporting standards. Critically, TekCollectXXXX reported this alleged debt to the credit bureaus before ever sending me a bill or validation notice. This violates the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1692g ), which requires collectors to provide written validation of a debt within 5 days of first contact, and prohibits collection activity ( including credit reporting ) until validation is given. The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau has explicitly confirmed this in its official bulletin, stating : > A debt collectors reporting of a debt to a consumer reporting agency is a collection activity that must not be done without providing the validation notice and giving the consumer an opportunity to exercise their rights. ( CFPB Bulletin XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX ). Courts have also upheld this interpretation. For example, in XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. XXXX XXXX ( XXXX XXXX XXXX ), affd, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ( XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX ), the court held that reporting a disputed debt to a credit bureau without first validating it constituted collection activity under the FDCPA. Similarly, in XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX. XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ( XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX ), the Sixth Circuit recognized that credit reporting is a powerful tool used by debt collectors and is indeed subject to the FDCPAs protections. At the state level, New Mexico courts have also emphasized strong consumer protections under the Unfair Practices Act ( XXXX XXXX, XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX ). In XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX ( XXXX ), the New Mexico Supreme Court held that businesses engage in an unfair or deceptive trade practice when they make representations that may, tend to, or do deceive or mislead any person. XXXX marketing of a Lifetime Smile Guarantee without disclosing how or when it could be voided, and its subsequent failure to honor that promise, clearly falls within this prohibited conduct under New Mexico law. Therefore, TekCollect and XXXX acted unlawfully by placing a derogatory mark on my credit file before ever providing me with proper notice or validation of the debt. This deprived me of my statutory right to dispute the debt before damage to my credit was done. -- - Appropriate and Requested Remedial Actions 1. Immediate Removal of Derogatory Credit Reporting Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ), furnishers of credit information must not report information they know or should reasonably know is inaccurate. There is no valid debt owed for services that were never rendered, and continued reporting of this balance is inaccurate, misleading, and legally unenforceable. I request that all derogatory marks related to this account be deleted from my credit file, pursuant to FCRA 1681i ( a ) ( 5 ) ( A ). 2. Cease and Desist Collection Efforts Attempting to collect a debt based on undelivered services and false promisesparticularly when the business is bankruptis a violation of the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), 15 U.S.C. 1692e ( 2 ) ( A ), which prohibits false representations about the legal status of a debt. TekCollect has never called me, and the only notice I received was an unsolicited email with no supporting documentation, violating FDCPA 1692g, which requires clear validation of debt upon first contact. I formally request a cease of all collection efforts and consider any future attempts unlawful until validation is produced. 3. Full Refund for Undelivered Services and Misrepresented Guarantees XXXX failed to complete treatment, withheld funds for undelivered retainers, and marketed a Lifetime Guarantee they never intended to honor. These failures constitute : Breach of Contract Unjust Enrichment Failure of Consideration ( Restatement ( Second ) of Contracts 237 ) Deceptive Practices under the FTC Act Violations of the New Mexico Unfair Practices Act ( XXXX XXXX, XXXX et seq., as applied in XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ). Because I must now seek care from another aligner company to complete treatment, I am incurring new out-of-pocket costs that should have been covered by XXXX original contract and falsely advertised guarantees. I request a full refund for all services not rendered, including the undelivered retainers. -- - Conclusion and Relief Sought In summary, I respectfully ask that the CFPB take the following actions : Instruct XXXX and/or HFD to remove all derogatory marks related to this debt ; Order a full cease of collection activity against me ; Ensure a complete refund is issued for the undelivered treatment and retainers ; Investigate SmileDirectClubs advertising and partner billing practices, particularly the misuse of Lifetime Guarantee language, the failure to disclose any lawful basis for voiding such a warranty, and the post-bankruptcy sale or transfer of consumer accounts. Thank you for your attention to this matter and for protecting consumers from exploitative, deceptive, and unlawful financial practices. Sincerely, XXXX XXXX

narrative: What happened in this situation is a clear case of identity theft, unauthorized use of my personal information, and the reporting of an account that does not belong to me. The Target/TD Bank account currently appearing on my credit report was not opened by me, was not authorized by me, and does not reflect any legitimate financial activity that I engaged in. I have also notified the credit bureaus and the furnisher that this account is fraudulent and must be removed under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ). I am creating this new case because the previous case did not result in proper correction, removal, or acknowledgment of the fraudulent nature of this account. This filing is intended to clearly document the facts, provide full compliance-related information, and ensure the company and credit bureaus understand that I do not own this account and am not responsible for any transactions, balances, late payments, or negative activity connected to it. 1. I Have Never Applied for or Opened a Target/TD Bank Account At no time did I complete a credit application, enter into an agreement, consent to terms, initiate an online request, or provide authorization for a Target/TD Bank account. I have no history of attempting to obtain credit with Target, nor have I used a Target credit card for any purchase. I have not received emails, letters, physical cards, billing statements, or account updates that would come from a legitimate account holder relationship. When I discovered this account on my credit report, it immediately raised red flags because it did not match any legitimate activity I have ever conducted. The fraudulent nature of the account is consistent with patterns of identity theft in which an unauthorized individual uses stolen information to open retail credit accounts without the victims knowledge. This appears to be exactly what happened here. 2. The FTC Identity Theft Report Confirms the Fraudulent Activity Once I realized this account was fraudulent, I immediately filed an official FTC Identity Theft Report, which is recognized under federal law as legal documentation of identity theft. This report establishes : I did not open the Target/TD Bank account I did not authorize the account I did not make any purchases connected to the account I am disputing the account under FCRA identity-theft protections I am requesting the full removal of this fraudulent information Under FCRA 605B ( Block of Information Resulting From Identity Theft ), once a consumer submits an FTC Identity Theft Report, the furnisher and bureaus are required to block and remove all information connected to the identity theft. Despite fulfilling this requirement, the account remains on my credit file, which is why I am escalating this matter through the CFPB. 3. This Fraudulent Account Has Caused Serious Harm to My Credit Profile This Target/TD Bank account has negatively impacted my credit in multiple ways : A. Lowered credit score The presence of derogatory information including late payments, delinquency status, or charged-off activity that I did not cause has lowered my credit score. This harms my ability to obtain legitimate credit, rental opportunities, important financial products, and even employment opportunities that consider creditworthiness. B. False representation of my payment history This fraudulent account creates the appearance that I mishandled credit, which is not accurate. I did not incur the debt, did not create the balance, and did not miss payments because I never opened the account in the first place. C. Increased credit utilization Any balance reported on the fraudulent account inflates my utilization ratio, which unfairly penalizes me under credit scoring models. D. Long-term damage to my credit file The continued reporting of fraudulent information affects my financial future. If the account is not removed promptly, the damage compounds over time. Under FCRA 602, consumer reporting agencies must maintain the maximum possible accuracy of information. Reporting fraudulent accounts violates that obligation. 4. This reflects a systemic failure and an unwillingness to correct harm caused by their own noncompliance. Subject : Complaint Against BANK OF AMERICA , N.A . for Violations of HJR 192, Public Law 73-10, UCC Provisions, Federal Regulations, U.S. Codes, and Unlawful Closure of Accounts Dear Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ), I am filing this formal complaint against BANK OF AMERICA , N.A . for numerous violations of my rights, including but not limited to : failure to honor lawful payment instruments, improper retention of securities, violation of UCC and holder-in-due-course laws, breaches of federal regulations and U.S. Codes, unlawful closure of accounts, and potential theft, fraud, language fraud, and securities fraud. These violations contradict House Joint Resolution 192 ( HJR 192 ), Public Law 73-10 ( Emergency Banking Act ), the Uniform Commercial Code ( UCC ), the U.S. Constitution, and various federal laws and regulations. Detailed Summary of Violations : Failure to Honor Securities and Lawful Payment Instruments : I tendered lawful payments using securities and negotiable instruments provided by BANK OF AMERICA, N.A., such as bills, statements, equity checks, bearer bonds, and coupons attached to the statements. According to UCC 3-104 ( a ) and UCC 3-302 ( a ) ( 2 ), these instruments are valid as negotiable instruments, and I accepted these securities " for value, '' issuing a restrictive endorsement as outlined in UCC 3-206. Additionally, I affixed postage stamps ( lawful money ) to these securities under HJR 192 and UCC 1-201 ( b ) ( 24 ), reinforcing my payments. Despite receiving these securities through registered and certified mail, BANK OF AMERICA , N.A . failed to discharge the debt, return the securities, or properly credit my account, in violation of UCC 3-603 ( b ). This provision mandates that any obligation is discharged to the extent of a payment made by a negotiable instrument unless that instrument is returned or dishonored. Their retention of the securities without action violates my rights as both a creditor and holder of the instruments. Unlawful Closure of Accounts and Definition of " Accounts '' : It is important to clarify that the term account inherently means a place for deposits and withdrawals, not a static or limited financial agreement. As such, BANK OF AMERICA , N.A . unlawfully closed my accounts even after I had discharged the related debts through the lawful tender of securities. These accounts, by their nature, should be considered open-ended credit plans, which should not have a predetermined limit. To : Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ) From : XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX # XXXX XXXX, GA XXXX XXXX XXXX Subject : Formal Complaint Against CKS Prime Investments , LLC ________________________________________ Background and Complaint Summary I am filing this formal complaint to address serious concerns with the reporting practices of CKS Prime Investments , LLC ( CKS Prime ). A debt attributed to me, with an open balance of {$700.00}, is reported under this entity as placed for collection and marked disputed. Despite my good-faith efforts to seek validation and clarification, CKS Prime has failed to produce adequate documentation or substantiation to support the legitimacy of this debt. CKS Prime has not provided : 1. A copy of the original agreement signed by me that establishes my liability for this debt. 2. A detailed and itemized statement of the debt, including the basis for any interest, fees, or charges assessed. 3. A clear and complete chain of title proving that CKS Prime has legal ownership and the authority to collect the alleged debt. Their inaction and lack of transparency raise significant concerns regarding compliance with federal and state consumer protection laws. ________________________________________ Legal Framework and Apparent Violations CKS Primes failure to respond appropriately and substantiate this debt appears to be in violation of several key consumer protection laws, including but not limited to : Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ) 15 U.S.C. 1692g ( Debt Validation and Verification ) : This statute requires debt collectors to provide, upon request, sufficient validation of a debt, including a copy of the original signed agreement. CKS Prime has not fulfilled this obligation. 15 U.S.C. 1692e ( False or Misleading Representations ) : Reporting or attempting to collect a debt without adequate proof constitutes deceptive and misleading behavior. Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( Responsibilities of Furnishers of Information ) : Credit furnishers are required to ensure that all reported debts are accurate, verifiable, and substantiated. The continued reporting of an unverified debt suggests a breach of this duty. 15 U.S.C. 1681c ( Obsolete Information ) : This provision limits how long negative information, such as a debt in collections, may remain on a credit report. The absence of clarity regarding the Date of First Delinquency raises additional questions about compliance. State-Specific Legal Violations ( Georgia ) Georgia Fair Business Practices Act ( FBPA ) : Prohibits unfair or deceptive acts or practices in consumer transactions, including the misrepresentation or lack of substantiation of debts. ________________________________________ Evidence of Procedural and Substantive Deficiencies Based on my review of the account reported by CKS Prime, I have identified the following procedural and substantive deficiencies : 1. Failure to Validate the Debt : CKS Prime has not provided legally required validation or documentation to establish my liability or the legitimacy of the debt. 2. Deficien t XXXX XXXX Compliance : The reporting appears to lack adherence to XXXX XXXX credit reporting standards, further raising doubts about its accuracy. 3. Ambiguity in Ownership and Authorization : No clear chain of title has been provided to demonstrate that CKS Prime has legal authority to collect or report this debt. ________________________________________ Relief and Remedial Action Sought In light of these issues, I respectfully request that the CFPB : 1. Investigate CKS Prime Investments , LLC : Conduct a thorough review of their debt collection and reporting practices to determine compliance with federal and state laws. 2. Demand Full Validation of the Debt : Compel CKS Prime to produce the following : o A signed original agreement establishing my liability for the debt. o A detailed account history of the debt. o A comprehensive chain of title showing all transfers of ownership or assignment of the debt to CKS Prime. XXXX. Ensure Deletion of the Disputed Account : Require CKS Prime to remove the account from my credit reports if they fail to provide sufficient validation. 4. Impose Penalties for Non-Compliance : Enforce fines or other corrective actions if systemic violations are identified. ________________________________________ Conclusion The actions of CKS Prime Investments , LLC appear to undermine the integrity of credit reporting and debt collection practices, not only harming me but also potentially affecting other consumers. I urge the CFPB to investigate this matter and take appropriate action to ensure compliance and accountability. Thank you for your attention to this matter. I look forward to your response. Attachments : 1. ) Copy of my driver license 2. ) Copy of the trade line on my credit reports Sincerely, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX

On XX/XX/year>, at XXXX PM, I called Jefferson Capital Systems LLC at XXXX. My call lasted XXXX minutes and XXXX seconds. I initially spoke with a representative named XXXX and requested a debt validation letter to review before making payment. I fully intended to pay the account in full upon receipt of this letter, as I am actively working to repair my credit. Under the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), consumers have the right to request a debt validation letter without disputing the account. However, XXXX informed me that they would need to file a dispute with the original creditor before they could send the validation letter. I emphasized that I did not wish to dispute the account and only wanted the validation letter for my records. Nonetheless, she transferred me to another representative, XXXX. XXXX also insisted that a dispute with the original creditor was necessary to fulfill my request for a validation letter. When I restated my rights under the FDCPA, XXXX interrupted and repeatedly stated their policy, disregarding my clarification that the FDCPA permits consumers to request debt validation without filing a dispute. Relevant Sections of the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ) The FDCPA explicitly grants consumers rights related to debt validation, prohibits misrepresentation, and disallows unfair practices, which Jefferson Capital Systems LLC appears to have disregarded in my case : XXXX. Debt Validation ( 15 U.S.C. 1692g ) Under this provision, consumers have the right to request a validation notice at any point, regardless of whether a dispute has been filed. Debt collectors are required to provide this upon request, detailing the debt amount, the name of the creditor, and the consumers rights. 2. Consumer Rights under the FDCPA The FDCPA entitles consumers to request validation of the debt at any time. A consumer is not required to dispute the debt to obtain this information, making Jefferson Capitals requirement of filing a dispute incorrect and misleading. 3. Misrepresentation ( 15 U.S.C. 1692e ) This section prohibits debt collectors from using false or misleading representations in debt collection, which includes misrepresenting consumer rights under the FDCPA. Jefferson Capital Systems LLCs representatives provided misleading information by claiming that a dispute was necessary for debt validation. 4. Unfair Practices ( 15 U.S.C. 1692f ) Debt collectors are forbidden from employing unfair means to collect a debt. Requiring me to dispute the debt with the original creditor to receive validation constitutes an unfair practice and a violation of my rights. Additionally, I have previously requested a debt validation letter from another collection agency, XXXX, and they were able to provide it without requiring me to dispute the account. This demonstrates that Jefferson Capital Systems LLCs insistence on filing a dispute before providing a validation letter is not standard practice and further underscores their failure to respect my consumer rights under the FDCPA To support my claim, I am attaching screenshots of the call log and notes taken during our conversations, along with additional call logs from the past few days, which show multiple calls made to XXXX XXXX. This evidence demonstrates that I am actively working to address my debts and improve my credit, rather than avoiding my responsibilities.

Issue Whether XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ( XXXX ) violated the Telephone Consumer Protection Act ( TCPA ), the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), and New York debt collection laws by repeatedly contacting third parties despite explicit instructions not to do so and by ignoring the complainants stated preferred methods of communication. Rule Telephone Consumer Protection Act ( TCPA ) : Restricts unsolicited communications and mandates adherence to consumer contact preferences. Prohibits harassment via calls or messages, including the use of prerecorded messages or calls to unintended parties without consent. Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ) : Limits debt collectors from contacting third parties except for location information, and only under strict guidelines. Prohibits communication after receiving instructions to stop and bans any behavior that may be construed as harassment. New York Debt Collection Laws ( General Business Law 601 ) : Protects consumers and third parties from harassing, oppressive, or abusive debt collection practices. Requires compliance with communication limitations explicitly requested by the debtor. Application A. Preferred Contact Methods Ignored : The complainant informed XXXX to contact only via a specific phone number and email address. These instructions were ignored. No calls were made to the specified number, nor were any emails sent, violating the TCPA and FDCPAs requirement to honor consumer communication preferences. B. Unauthorized Third-Party Contacts : On XX/XX/year>, XXXX from XXXX left a voicemail with an associate of the complainant seeking location information. Despite a follow-up voicemail from the complainant on XX/XX/year>, directing XXXX to cease contacting associates, a similar voicemail was left with at least one other associate on XX/XX/year>. These actions contravene both the FDCPA and New York laws restricting third-party contact. C. Complainant Attempts to Resolve the Issue : On XX/XX/year>, the complainant left a voicemail on XXXX 's line, clearly stating that contacting associates would be considered harassment and providing explicit instructions for contact via phone and email. On XX/XX/year>, the complainant left another voicemail on XXXX 's line. This voicemail, which was recorded, stated that XXXX may only contact the complainant by way of the specified email. On XX/XX/year>, the complainant spoke directly with XXXX, a XXXX representative. During this conversation, the complainant reiterated that XXXX may only contact him via the specified email and/or phone number. He also emphasized that they are not allowed to contact any other associates, reaffirming his communication preferences. D. Business Management and Contact Information : According to the XXXX XXXX XXXX ( XXXX ), the President of XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX is XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. E. Repeated Violations and Evidence of Harassment : XXXX ignored these instructions and continued contacting associates, engaging in behavior amounting to harassment. The complainant will present evidence, including : Voicemail Recordings : Voicemails left by " XXXX '' on associates ' phones, illustrating unauthorized third-party contact. Phone Call Recordings : Recordings of calls between the complainant and XXXX representatives, pre-authorized by the parties involved. These recordings document the complainants clear instructions and XXXX acknowledgment of the restrictions. Email Communication : A copy of the demand letter sent to XXXX email address outlining the allegations and specifying contact restrictions. Preferred Outcome The complainant seeks the following outcomes : XXXX immediately ceases all violations of the TCPA, FDCPA, and New York debt collection laws. XXXX adheres to the complainants specified communication preferences, contacting only via the email address and phone number provided in the demand letter, two voicemails, and the verbal conversation with XXXX. XXXX stops all harassment via calls or messages. XXXX prohibits further communication with the complainants associates under any circumstances. Conclusion XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX violated the TCPA, FDCPA, and New York debt collection laws by : Failing to adhere to the complainants specified communication methods. Persistently contacting third parties in direct violation of the complainants instructions. Engaging in harassing behavior through repeated unauthorized communications. The complainant has substantial evidence, including voicemail recordings, phone call recordings, and email correspondence, to substantiate claims of harassment and statutory violations.

I am filing this complaint against Midland Credit Management ( MCM ) for their failure to adhere to the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), and the principles of the Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ) in their handling of an alleged debt they claim I owe. Failure to Validate Debt ( Violating FDCPA 809 ( a ) ) : I sent two certified letters to MCM requesting validation of the alleged debt, as mandated by the FDCPA, specifically under 809 ( a ). Despite these requests, MCM has failed to provide any such validation or documentation proving my obligation to pay the alleged debt. These requests were made on XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX, with USPS tracking confirming their delivery. Unauthorized Collection Actions Without Providing Debt Validation ( Violating FDCPA 809 ( b ) ) : Despite my requests for validation, MCM proceeded with collection actions, in direct violation of 809 ( b ) of the FDCPA, which stipulates that collection activities must cease until the debt is validated. Lack of Notice Regarding Debt Sale ( Impacting Rights Under FCRA and TILA Principles ) : I received no notification of the debt 's sale to MCM, a practice that seems contrary to the transparency and accuracy required by the FCRA, specifically 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( a ), which mandates the furnishing of accurate credit information, and principles under TILA, which emphasize the importance of informed consent and disclosure of significant financial information to consumers. Ignored Attempts for Information ( Undermining FCRA 611 and FDCPA Principles ) : My attempts to obtain information regarding this debt have been consistently ignored by MCM. This behavior not only contravenes the FDCPA 's mandates for fair debt collection practices but also undermines the FCRA 's 611 provision, which gives consumers the right to dispute and obtain information about the accuracy of information reported to credit reporting agencies. As of this correspondence MCM has not provided the original contract, terms of agreement, proof of reassignment of the debt, and other supporting documentation required by law. I urge the CFPB to take immediate action against Midland Credit Management for these violations and to ensure that my consumer rights are upheld in accordance with federal law.

I have also emailed CARRINGTON 'S OWN ADVOCATES DEPT. ( XX/XX/23 and XX/XX/23 ), WITH NO RESPONSE.!!!! Cognitive dissonance warning ahead!!!! I was told NO ONE WILL even ASK that the funds be reversed from principal, UNLESS AND UNTIL I pay another partial payment of {$48000.00} ( asked pre-due date ), and even then, all they could promise was to ASK someone, somewhere, IF the {$1000.00} can be reversed with NO GUARANTEE, along with no guarantee that my additional {$480.00} won't also be misapplied to principal, because it is also a " partial payment, '' which is the reason I was given for why the {$1000.00} was put toward principal in the first place! NO REMEDY : So being that my mortgage payment was due today, I went ahead and made the recommended partial payment of {$480.00}. It felt like I was being extorted for more money from CARRINGTON who already seemed to mismanage my other funds, with no assurances of a positive outcome, and not knowing HOW LONG it might take to get a decision from CARRINGTON, running scared that my mortgage payment runs the risk of either being " late '' or of me having to come up with another supplemental amount, before that happens, which would surely put an undue financial burden on me. The reason I was in arrears in the first place was due to a combination of a COVID hardship and a prolonged health issue. I am presently on XXXX, and have NO EXTRA INCOME to make EXTRA mortgage payments, and IF I DID have any unassigned money I certainly would be paying it to my other bills that are due and owing, and not to the principal on my mortgage loan. That is not a luxury I can afford at this time. ACCOUNTABILITY : Aren't there laws or regulations governing against this type of treatment of customer funds? If so, why isn't CARRINGTON aware of them? And is there a way to hold them accountable? I read tonight that a bank has NO fiduciary responsibility to a customer. I couldn't believe it. How is that possible? They are not to " mismanage '' funds but I'm guessing THAT word can be defined in a way advantageous to CARRINGTON or other banks, or maybe be unclear, or maybe they are simply counting on being protected somehow. It just doesn't seem right. CLOSING : I usually don't make a complaint when I receive bad customer service. Everyone can have a bad day or not have been given enough training or be short-staffed, so ok. However, in this case, it seems more about who controls what we are led to believe is our money. Isn't it MY money? I mean I put it there with a very specific intention of using it to make a mortgage payment. Do banks really have that much power over our money? If so, that is very scary, and we need to speak up about this kind of thing. People can't fight against what they don't know exists. I am just trying to pay my mortgage so I can keep my house which is already difficult enough to do. Anything the CFPB can do will be greatly appreciated. Thank you!

I did not want to give up my unlocked phone, but I felt unsafe and cornered and did not object as I did not know what they would do to me otherwise. They also handed me a clipboard with a sheet for me to fill in my info during this time, and held my phone away from me so I could not see what they were doing on it. I attempted to look at what they were doing on my phone multiple times but they held it just out of my view. After making the charge, they gave me back my card and phone and left. Their behavior with my phone made me suspicious, so as soon as I got in my car, I checked the charges on my card and saw that there was a charge for {$5000.00} to XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, which is a merchant I had never heard of and a charge that was grossly in excess of what I agreed to donate. I later looked online and could not find any evidence of the merchant existing. I also checked my text messages to see if there was a verification or notification XXXX that had been sent or responded to, but could not find XXXX ; I assume that XXXX was sent that they quickly responded to and deleted. I immediately called the Chase fraud line to get my card locked and I let the associate know what had happened. He said that he would cancel my card, get a new one sent to me, and put a note on my account. He also told me that the charge would be reversed in about 48 hours, which it was. I was shaking and scared for the entire rest of the day, and this was compounded by the fact that I had not thought to write fake personal information down on the clipboard they gave me and for a while I was very scared that they might try to follow me or come to my home upon finding out that Id canceled the card. Ive been too scared to go out into the city alone since then as well. The charge was added back onto my account. I disputed the charge, as at no point did I agree to pay the amount that was charged to my card. This was a scam that intentionally abused the fact that I was a woman alone in the dark, confronted and cornered by three men - XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX As soon as I received the letter from Chase that denied my fraud claim, I called again to try to figure out what further steps I could take as at that point I was very confused. I felt I had done everything right in calling the fraud department minutes after the event transpired and getting my card canceled. They directed me to the disputes department, and when I called that department they informed me that I had to type and send a physical letter to their customer service office to open a dispute, alongside any more information I wished to provide. I promptly did so ; this letter is a slightly modified and updated version of the letter I sent to the Chase customer service department. I received a response from Chase on XX/XX/XXXX in the form of another letter that said they had resolved my dispute. I have attached this letter below, but the gist of it is that they found that I either received the services or the merchant made them available for my use and they cant confirm Im due a credit because the services I purchased were received or available to use. By this point I was extremely upset and confused, especially since the amount that they fraudulently charged me for was an amount that was, and still is, lowering my credit score as it accounts for over half of the limit on my credit card. On XX/XX/XXXX I went into a local Chase branch to try to get this situation resolved. I explained what had happened to the representative who met with me, and she was immediately sympathetic after hearing me out and reading my written statement ( the same one I had sent to the customer service office a few weeks prior ). She advised me to get a police report written up about the situation, which I had not thought to do prior as I was extremely shaken after the events initially transpired and thought that reporting things to the fraud department and getting my card canceled would be enough. I went to a local police station that same day and met with an officer, who wrote up a police report on the events and gave me a copy to give to the Chase representative, which I did later that day. I received another notice from Chase on XX/XX/XXXX asking for further information on my dispute, which again confused me as Id provided every document and piece of evidence that I had up until that point. I booked another appointment with the Chase representative who I had met with earlier and met with her again on XX/XX/XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX She did her best to help me dispute the transaction and get the charge lifted from my card, but to no avail. Ultimately, the system that had the final say was not something she had any control over, and despite her best efforts, Chase again determined that the disputed transaction was valid and sent me a letter saying so on XX/XX/XXXX. In addition, the event itself is something I hate being forced to constantly recall as it makes me feel very scared and unsafe whenever I think about it. I am very upset about how Ive been treated by Chase throughout this entire process, and I am sick and tired of still having to deal with this event almost six months after it transpired. I feel that I have exhausted all other options without getting anywhere, which is why I am now filing a complaint through the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau.
